injuryReports.name: Isaiah Adams
injuryReports.returnComment: Adams was placed on IR in early October and missed the required four games. He was designated to return Wednesday and was limited in all three of Arizona's practices this week. Now that he's been activated, Adams is eligible to suit up Sunday, and if he returns he'll likely reclaim his starting role at right guard.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Shawn Bowman
injuryReports.returnComment: Bowman was previously elevated for Week 6, when he logged four snaps on special teams (and none on offense) against the Rams. His usage could be similarly limited Sunday against Seattle, as the Cardinals have three healthy tight ends (Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Teagan Quitoriano) ahead of Bowman in the pecking order.
injuryReports.injury: Arizona elevated Bowman from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Jerome Ford
injuryReports.returnComment: Ford signed with Arizona's practice squad Oct. 14 and is now set to potentially make his gameday debut with the team Sunday in Seattle. He spent his first four NFL campaigns with Cleveland and averaged an acceptable 4.3 yards per carry with seven rushing touchdowns over 340 totes while also accumulating 647 yards and an additional five touchdowns on 107 catches across 57 games. Given that level of experience, it will be interesting to see how much the Cardinals utilize Ford on Sunday, though Tyler Allgeier is slated to work as the team's lead back, and Evan Hull will also factor into the mix.
injuryReports.injury: The Cardinals elevated Ford from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Jon Gaines II
injuryReports.returnComment: Gaines continues to battle a knee injury and will miss his third straight game. Hayden Conner may make another start at right guard, though Isaiah Adams (ankle) -- who has been deemed questionable -- could take on that role if he's activated from IR on Saturday.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jayden Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams made an early exit from Sunday's loss to Dallas after hurting his knee. He didn't practice at all this week and is set to miss the first game of his career. The rookie has started four of Arizona's first eight contests of the campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Walter Nolen III
injuryReports.returnComment: An ankle injury caused Nolen to miss Arizona's past two contests, but he was able to log a trio of limited practices this week. That gives him at least a chance of suiting up Sunday in Seattle. Should Nolen need to sit out again, though, L.J. Collier could soak up most of his defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Max Melton
injuryReports.returnComment: Melton missed Week 7 versus Denver due to a knee issue but was able to return last Sunday against Dallas. However, the injury is still a concern, and the third-year cornerback was limited in practice both Thursday and Friday this week. If he can't play in Week 9, Kalen King may log a start.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Michael Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson has worn a yellow non-contact jersey in practice the last two weeks due to two broken ribs -- a situation that contained him to limited sessions. Having said that, he'll continue to play through the concern as he did this past Sunday in Dallas, when he hauled in eight of 15 targets for 111 yards and one touchdown while adding one carry for 17 yards on a 79 percent snap share.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson (rest/ribs) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest in Seattle, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Bam Knight
injuryReports.returnComment: After being concussed early in last Sunday's game against Dallas, Knight will miss at least one contest, as he remains in the league's protocol. With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) also sidelined, Tyler Allgeier projects to handle most of the backfield work, though it's a really tough road draw against a strong run defense.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Elijah Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: Wideout Michael Wilson missed a portion of the contest due to an injury to his ribs, and Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) exited for good late in the first half. That resulted in a need for other Cardinals pass catchers to step up, and Higgins ended up getting targeted a season-high four times. However, he didn't do much with the opportunity, finishing with his lowest yardage total since he was shut out in Week 2. Meanwhile, No. 1 tight end Trey McBride had another big game with seven catches for 72 yards and a touchdown on eight targets. McBride's elite status will likely continue to make Higgins an afterthought most weeks.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins tallied two catches for 10 yards on four targets Sunday in a 33-30 overtime win over Dallas.

injuryReports.name: Reggie Virgil
injuryReports.returnComment: Virgil played a season-high 38 offensive snaps, but he went without a reception for the third straight week. The Cardinals placed Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) on injured reserve Tuesday after the wide receiver fractured his right tibia in Week 8, so more opportunities could come Virgil's way moving forward. Regardless of an increase in workload, the team's Week 9 matchup versus Seattle will be a challenging one for the 22-year-old.
injuryReports.injury: Virgil failed to reel in either of his targets during Sunday's 33-30 overtime victory against Dallas.

injuryReports.name: Devin Duvernay
injuryReports.returnComment: Duvernay reeled in his first two passes of the year while playing 34 offensive snaps in the victory. Fellow wideout Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) fractured his right tibia during the contest, and he is likely set to miss the rest of the 2026 campaign. Duvernay will likely see an increased role on offense in Bourne's absence, but he will remain an unappealing fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup against Seattle.
injuryReports.injury: Duvernay caught both of his targets for 14 yards while also adding 75 yards as a kick returner and 12 punt-return yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime win against the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Simi Fehoko
injuryReports.returnComment: Buried on the depth chart at receiver to begin the season, Fehoko mostly served as a special-teams contributor through the Cardinals' first seven games. However,the Cardinals have since traded away Marvin Harrison before losing Jalen Brooks (wrist) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) to season-ending injuries within the past two weeks, so Fehoko suddenly finds himself in a position to contribute. Fehoko played double-digit snaps for the first time in 2026 on Sunday, coincidentally against his former teams the Cowboys. He wasn't much of a factor in a comeback win, however, earning just one target for a 17-yard reception while taking the field for 40 of the team's 81 offensive play. While Fehoko could see his playing time climb even higher in Week 9, tight ends Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins, wideout Michael Wilson (ribs) and running back Tyler Allgeier may be better bets to command targets from quarterback Gardner Minshew.
injuryReports.injury: Fehoko is listed as a starting receiver on the Cardinals' unofficial depth chart heading into Sunday's game at Seattle, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.

injuryReports.name: James Conner
injuryReports.returnComment: Though LaFleur said last week that Conner could "potentially" play this season, that won't happen in Week 9. The veteran running back continues to work his way back from a right foot injury and has not yet been cleared to practice. Arizona is dealing with multiple injuries in its backfield, including Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion), so Conner could provide a big boost once he's able to work his way back this week. Instead, the team will turn to Tyler Allgeier to lead its backfield, with Evan Hull serving as his primary backup if Knight is unable to suit up Sunday against Seattle.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Tyler Allgeier
injuryReports.returnComment: After previously leading the Cardinals backfield when Love was sidelined due to a different ankle injury Weeks 6 and 7, Allgeier is now slated for a longer run atop the depth chart while Love is projected to miss 4-to-5 weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain. Love sustained his latest ankle injury late in the first quarter of Sunday's overtime win over the Cowboys, with his early exit clearing the way for Allgeier to run wild. Allgeier finished with a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries along with 44 yards and another score on five receptions. In addition to Love getting hurt, Bam Knight sustained a concussion and is uncertain to play Week 9 against Seattle, so the backfield could belong to Allgeier, Evan Hull and a practice-squad signee (likely Jerome Ford). Though Allgeier found substantial success in Week 8, he came into the contest averaging just 2.9 yards per carry on 61 totes. He'll also be facing a Seattle defense that is tied for the second-fewest yards per carry (3.8) allowed to running backs this season, so a repeat performance by Allgeier would be surprising.
injuryReports.injury: Allgeier is slated to work as Arizona's No. 1 running back beginning with Sunday's game at Seattle after Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Harrison Wallace III
injuryReports.returnComment: Wallace signed to Arizona's practice squad in August and has yet to play in a regular-season game. Week 9 will be the undrafted free agent's NFL debut should he be active for Sunday's matchup against Seattle. He will likely act as a depth piece should he play.
injuryReports.injury: The Cardinals signed Wallace from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.

injuryReports.name: Jeremiyah Love
injuryReports.returnComment: Love's move to IR was fully expected, after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported earlier Tuesday that the rookie first-round pick was diagnosed with a right high-ankle sprain and was facing a projected recovery timeline of 4-to-5 weeks. While Love is on the mend, Tyler Allgeier is expected to step into a lead role out of the Arizona backfield beginning with the team's Week 9 game against Seattle.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Kendrick Bourne
injuryReports.returnComment: Though Bourne is expected to avoid surgery after fracturing his right tibia during Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys, he's facing an expected recovery timeline of three months that effectively ends his season. With Bourne heading to IR, the Cardinals signed Harrison Wallace off their practice squad to replenish their depth at receiver. The 31-year-old Bourne will finish the 2026 campaign with 26 receptions for 263 yards and no touchdowns on 38 targets over eight appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Lower Leg

injuryReports.name: Chad Ryland
injuryReports.returnComment: Ryland's missed PAT came in the fourth quarter with 1:03 remaining after Michael Wilson's touchdown knotted the game at 30-30. Arizona was lucky to get to overtime, but Ryland made the winning kick with 4:09 remaining, drilling a 42-yard field goal. On the season, he's made 19 of 21 field-goal tries and 16 of 17 extra-point attempts.
injuryReports.injury: Ryland converted both of his field-goal attempts and three of four PATs in Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Carson Beck
injuryReports.returnComment: Beck had been a healthy inactive through each of the Cardinals' first eight games of the season as the emergency No. 3 quarterback, but he'll get the chance to dress for the first time in Week 9 after Arizona removed the struggling Jacoby Brissett from the starting role and dropped him down two spots on the depth chart. Like Brissett, the 30-year-old Minshew is a journeyman who isn't viewed as the team's long-term solution under center, so it wouldn't be surprising if Beck eventually received a look as the starter before the end of the season if Arizona eventually fades from playoff contention. A rookie third-round pick out of Miami, Beck completed 15 of 19 pass attempts for 188 yards and a touchdown during his lone preseason appearance.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Mike LaFleur said that Beck will serve as the Cardinals' No. 2 quarterback behind starter Gardner Minshew in Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Gardner Minshew II
injuryReports.returnComment: Unsurprisingly, the Cardinals have opted to appoint Minshew to the top spot on the depth chart after he came on in relief of a struggling Jacoby Brissett and led a stirring comeback in Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys. In what was his first appearance of the season, Minshew completed 17 of 23 pass attempts for 188 yards and three touchdowns in just under two quarters' worth of action before Chad Ryland sealed the victory with a walk-off 42-yard field goal. Though his performance in future games will ultimately dictate how long he sticks around as the Cardinals' starter, Minshew is far from a lock to hold down the job for the balance of the season. If the 3-5 Cardinals eventually fade from playoff contention, LaFleur may want to give an extended look to rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who will serve as Minshew's top backup in Week 9 while Brissett falls to third on the depth chart, per Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Mike LaFleur announced that Minshew will step in as the Cardinals' new starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game at Seattle, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

injuryReports.name: Alec Anderson
injuryReports.returnComment: Anderson didn't practice Thursday or Friday due to an ankle injury, but he was able to log a limited session Saturday to have at least a chance of suiting up Monday. If Anderson ends up being sidelined, Austin Corbett could draw the start at left guard.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Spencer Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Brown missed last Sunday's win over Baltimore, but he'll be back in action Monday after logging an LP/LP/FP practice progression this week. His return will be especially critical if fellow starting offensive tackle Dion Dawkins (ribs, questionable) isn't able to suit up.
injuryReports.injury: Brown (back) does not have a designation for Monday's matchup in Minnesota.

injuryReports.name: Dion Dawkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Dawkins didn't practice at all this week due to an injury to his ribs, but he still has a chance to suit up. Per Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News, the veteran tackle was hurt in the first half of last Sunday's win over Baltimore but was able to finish out the contest. Dawkins said he'll do everything he can to be ready for Monday Night Football, so he may be a true game-time decision.
injuryReports.injury: Ribs

injuryReports.name: Tyrell Shavers
injuryReports.returnComment: Shavers remains on the reserve/PUP list with a knee injury despite logging three consecutive full practices during Week 9 prep. The wide receiver could return to the active roster ahead of Monday night's showdown with the Vikings, but it will be contingent on the Bills creating a spot on the 53-man roster in time.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - ACL

injuryReports.name: Keon Coleman
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News, Coleman again was spotted in a red non-contact jersey Saturday and eventually went down as a limited participant for a third consecutive practice. Despite the restrictions this week, though, Coleman is ready to suit up for an eighth straight game to begin the season, having put up a 20-287-3 line on 27 targets to date.
injuryReports.injury: Coleman (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's contest in Minnesota.

injuryReports.name: DJ Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: While logging three straight limited practices during Week 9 prep, Moore continued to wear a red non-contact jersey due to the AC joint sprain that he's been dealing with since Week 2. Now that he's in the clear for Monday's matchup, he'll look to build upon the 16-260-2 line on 27 targets that he's racked up through five eppearances on the campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Moore (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's contest at Minnesota.

injuryReports.name: Joshua Palmer
injuryReports.returnComment: Palmer exited last Sunday's win against the Ravens in the first half and wasn't able to return due to a hamstring injury. After not practicing Thursday or Friday, the Bills opted to keep him on the sidelines in Week 9, meaning Greg Dortch, Skyler Bell and/or Tyrell Shavers (knee, IR) may see WR reps behind the team's top trio at the position.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Ty Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: A quick return after Thursday's absence confirms Johnson isn't dealing with a serious illness. He should be fine for his usual role on passing downs Monday night at Minnesota.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson (illness) was a full practice participant Friday.

injuryReports.name: Dalton Kincaid
injuryReports.returnComment: Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo previously noted that Kincaid had shed his red non-contact jersey at Friday's practice, and the tight end's full participation in the session paves the way for him to be in uniform Monday night against the Vikings. Over his last two games, Kincaid (who overall is tied for first among Bills in catches (27) and leads the team in receiving yards (401)) has logged an 11-124-1 receiving line, a pace that keeps him relevant from a fantasy perspective.
injuryReports.injury: Kincaid (chest) was a full participant in Friday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Dee Alford
injuryReports.returnComment: Alford was inactive for Sunday's win over the Ravens, though it appears he will be back on the field when the Bills face the Vikings on Monday night. With the 28-year-old back in the equation, Te'Cory Couch and Maxwell Hairston will likely see fewer snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Alford (ankle) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Hancock
injuryReports.returnComment: Hancock has been on IR since late September while recovering from a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 2 versus Detroit. The cornerback had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, and if he isn't activated in that time frame, he will remain on IR for the rest of the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Greg Gaines
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Dawson Knox
injuryReports.returnComment: It's a typical receiving line for Knox, whose main contributions come in the blocking department. Knox has nine grabs for 42 yards and one touchdown across seven appearances this season. He'd likely need multiple wideout and tight-end injuries to be a fantasy consideration.
injuryReports.injury: Knox caught one of two targets for six yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Ray Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: With the Bills throttling the Ravens and James Cook suffering a neck injury late in the game, Davis got some added run in the fourth quarter. If Cook misses any time, Davis would be the likely early-down replacement, with Ty Johnson sticking to his role on passing downs and four- and two-minute situations.
injuryReports.injury: Davis rushed six times for 30 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Bass
injuryReports.returnComment: Bass converted multiple long-range field goals for the Bills after the offense stalled several times due to drops. The kicker succeeded from 56 yards, 22 yards and 51 yards in the contest. Bass has converted all 16 of his field-goal attempts and is 21-for-23 on PATs through seven games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Bass made all three of his field-goal attempts as well as three PATs in the Bills' 36-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Greg Dortch
injuryReports.returnComment: Dortch has been serving as Buffalo's top return man throughout the season, but he continues to see limited involvement as a receiver. The 28-year-old hasn't played more than five offensive snaps in any of his seven appearances and has yet to draw a target.
injuryReports.injury: Dortch went without a target while logging four of the Bills' 82 snaps on offense in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. He returned one kickoff for 22 yards and three punts for 40 yards.

injuryReports.name: Khalil Shakir
injuryReports.returnComment: Shakir initially appeared to get in the end zone for a six-yard touchdown early in the first quarter, but he was ruled out at the one-yard line after review. Josh Allen then punched in the one-yard touchdown two plays later. On the day, Shakir paced the Bills with his five grabs and tied for second on the team in targets, one behind DJ Moore. Shakir has yet to hit 100 yards in a game this season and has just one touchdown, settling in as a low-ceiling WR4 in fantasy, especially when both Moore and Dalton Kincaid are healthy.
injuryReports.injury: Shakir caught five of six targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: James Cook III
injuryReports.returnComment: Cook gave the Bills some breathing room with a five-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to extend Buffalo's lead to 23-10. He was evaluated for a head injury later in the game but received clearance to return and notched one more carry after that point. After being held to 57 rushing yards without a touchdown by the Texans in Week 1, Cook has rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in six consecutive games. Extending that streak won't be easy in Week 9 against Minnesota's elite defense on MNF.
injuryReports.injury: Cook rushed 21 times for 80 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Josh Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen capped the opening drive with a one-yard touchdown plunge on which he went airborne to stretch the ball over the goal line. He struggled as a passer in the first half, including a first-quarter interception, but Allen heated up after halftime to post his highest passing yards total since a 334-yard Week 1 performance. Allen's 11-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore (knee) in the fourth quarter gave Allen sole possession of first place in Bills history with 259 passing touchdowns, including postseason play. He added a 23-yard touchdown pass to Dalton Kincaid on the next drive as the Bills pulled away from a Ravens team that lost top two QBs Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe). Allen has led the Bills to a 6-1 record heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the 6-1 Vikings.
injuryReports.injury: Allen completed 21 of 34 passes for 289 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. He added 30 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown on seven rushing attempts.

injuryReports.name: AJ Dillon
injuryReports.returnComment: It's the third straight week that Dillon is a healthy scratch, and he hasn't logged game-day action since Week 4 against Detroit. Meanwhile, rookie RB Anthony Tyus continues to be active, due largely to his work as a kick returner. As such, it appears Dillon isn't likely to suit up unless one of the RBs ahead of him in the pecking order -- Chuba Hubbard, Trevor Etienne or Tyus -- needs to miss time.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Haynes King
injuryReports.returnComment: King should be used to this role, as it's one he's had in each of Carolina's contests so far  this season. It has yet to yield a regular-season snap for the rookie out of Georgia Tech, and King will be eligible to enter Sunday's matchup only if both Bryce Young and Kenny Pickett exit due to injury, illness or ejection.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Bobby Okereke
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Jaelan Phillips
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Will Lee III
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Damien Lewis
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: TeRah Edwards
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Brady Christensen
injuryReports.returnComment: Christensen has been on injured reserve since Sept. 1. He was designated to return Tuesday and was a full participant in all three of Carolina's practices this week, but the Panthers aren't ready to activate him. Christensen's next chance to play is Sunday, Nov. 15, in New Orleans.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Marco Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson was elevated for the first time this season last weekend, and he ended up starting and logging every Panthers defensive snap against Green Bay. The veteran cornerback could do the same Sunday versus Denver, as Will Lee has been ruled out due to a hamstring injury and Akayleb Evans (triceps) is on IR. Wilson finished with eight tackles and two defensed passes in his Panthers debut.
injuryReports.injury: The Panthers elevated Wilson from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Bryce Young
injuryReports.returnComment: Young has been a full practice participant throughout the week, apparently not too bothered by a sore ankle. The bigger concern for Sunday is Denver's impressive pass rush matching up against Carolina's injury-riddled offensive line.
injuryReports.injury: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Friday that Young (ankle) is ready for Sunday's game against Denver after a "great week" of practice, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Bobby Brown III
injuryReports.returnComment: Brown missed last Thursday night's loss to the Packers but appears ready to return for Sunday's Week 9 date with Denver. He has seven tackles (one solo) and a pass breakup across 142 defensive snaps this season.
injuryReports.injury: Brown (hand) practiced fully Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Zakee Wheatley
injuryReports.returnComment: Wheatley was able to secure a career-high seven stops, while his biggest play of the game came in the fourth quarter when he picked off a deep pass from Packers quarterback Jordan Love. The interception was the first of the Wheatley's career, and the rookie has now compiled 26 total tackles (19 solo), four passes defensed and a forced fumble over six contests during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Wheatley recorded seven total tackles (four solo) and an interception during Thursday night's 27-19 loss to the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Jonathon Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: The Panthers haven't yet opened Brooks' 21-day practice window, but that might happen soon after head coach Dave Canales said Monday that the young running back would "potentially" be designated for return from injured reserve this week. Brooks hasn't played since Week 2 after undergoing core-muscle surgery, so he'll likely need to turn in multiple full practices before the Panthers are comfortable clearing him for game action. Once he's activated from IR, Brooks will likely handle a supporting role out of the backfield behind starter Chubba Hubbard.
injuryReports.injury: Abdomen

injuryReports.name: Darren Waller
injuryReports.returnComment: Waller has been hit or miss from a fantasy perspective this season, with two touchdown grabs in Week 2 in Atlanta and a 50-yard TD catch in Week 7 against the Buccaneers serving as the notable performances. Otherwise, he has one 50-yard effort in his five other appearances, sitting on a 15-209-3 line on 25 targets on the season. Waller next takes aim at the tough Broncos defense this coming Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Waller corralled one of two targets for 11 yards during last Thursday's 27-19 loss at Green Bay.

injuryReports.name: Xavier Legette
injuryReports.returnComment: Canales noted that Legette still has some checkpoints he needs to hit in his recovery process before getting the green light to practice, but the third-year wideout appears to have at least progressed on some level since landing on IR on Oct. 3. Before getting hurt, Legette had served as the Panthers' No. 3 wideout during the first two weeks of the season and produced a 2-64-0 receiving line on six targets between those contests.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Brycen Tremayne
injuryReports.returnComment: Tremayne took the field for 19 of the Panthers' 73 snaps on offense, with his 26-percent share marking his lowest rate since Week 2. The 26-year-old appears to have been passed up on the depth chart at receiver by John Metchie, who logged 33 snaps Thursday and has now had higher playing-time shares than Tremayne for three straight games.
injuryReports.injury: Tremayne finished with an 11-yard reception on his lone target in Thursday's 27-19 loss to the Packers.

injuryReports.name: John Metchie III
injuryReports.returnComment: Metchie took the field for 33 of the Panthers' 73 snaps on offense, placing him behind Tetairoa McMillan (65 snaps) and Jalen Coker (63) but ahead of Brycen Tremayne (19) and David Moore (zero) among Carolina receivers. Though he's now drawn at least three targets in five straight games, Metchie has found the end zone just once and is averaging 22.8 receiving yards per contest during that stretch.
injuryReports.injury: Metchie recorded three receptions for 14 yards on three targets in Thursday's 27-19 loss to the Packers.

injuryReports.name: David Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: After logging a season-high 13 snaps on offense a week earlier in the Panthers' blowout loss to the Buccaneers, Moore's playing time was contained to special teams while Carolina leaned exclusively on Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, Brycen Tremayne and John Metchie at receiver.
injuryReports.injury: Moore didn't receive any playing time on offense and logged two snaps on special teams in Thursday's 27-19 loss to the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
injuryReports.returnComment: Fitzgerald didn't attempt a kick in the Week 7 loss to Tampa Bay. The 26-year-old got back on the board Thursday, draining a 39-yard field goal early in the first quarter before capping off the night with a 50-yarder late in the third. Fitzgerald has made all 13 of his field goals this season, though he's missed five extra-point attempts.
injuryReports.injury: Fitzgerald made both field-goal attempts and converted his only extra-point try in Thursday's 27-19 loss to Green Bay.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Coker
injuryReports.returnComment: Coker was having a forgettable night before he used his speed to turn a short Bryce Young pass into a 26-yard touchdown with just under six minutes remaining in the contest. Coker's fumble came on the last play of the game, as he lost the handle on the ball shortly after receiving a lateral from Tetairoa McMillan at the Panthers' 26-yard line. Coker is in the midst of a two-game downturn that unsurprisingly coincides with struggles on the part of Bryce Young, as the speedy wideout has just three receptions for 45 yards and Thursday's score in that span heading into a tough Week 9 assignment at home against the Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 8.
injuryReports.injury: Coker secured two of five targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers' 27-19 loss to the Packers on Thursday. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Chuba Hubbard
injuryReports.returnComment: Hubbard was able to log his usual hefty workload despite Carolina trailing for large swaths of the contest, and the veteran back added his fifth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a one-yard run on the first play of the second quarter. He also led the Panthers in receptions with a season-high figure, and he now has seven total scores in seven games. Hubbard averaged under 4.0 yards per carry for the first time this season, but he's still clocking 4.6 yards per tote heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 8.
injuryReports.injury: Hubbard rushed 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown and brought in seven of eight targets for 38 yards in the Panthers' 27-19 loss to the Packers on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Tetairoa McMillan
injuryReports.returnComment: McMillan led the Panthers in receiving yards despite generating a modest total, and the second-year wideout has now fallen under 60 receiving yards in consecutive games for the first time this season. He does have at least six grabs in three of the past four games and a trio of double-digit target tallies on the season, so he continues to sport a formidable fantasy floor despite Bryce Young's current struggles. Carolina's air attack may have a tough time bouncing back in Week 9, however, as the stingy Broncos defense comes to town on Sunday, Nov. 8.
injuryReports.injury: McMillan brought in six of 11 targets for 57 yards in the Panthers' 27-19 loss to the Packers on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Tyrique Stevenson Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: A thumb injury left Stevenson uncertain for Week 9, and his availability will not officially be revealed until 90 minutes before Sunday's 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. However -- per the report -- with help from a splint, it appears he will be ready to take the field.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Malik Muhammad II
injuryReports.returnComment: Muhammad missed last week's victory over the Seahawks due to a toe injury sustained in Week 7, but it appears he will miss only the lone contest.
injuryReports.injury: Toe

injuryReports.name: Kyle Monangai
injuryReports.returnComment: Monangai was able to get back on the practice field Friday for the first time since suffering a turf-toe injury versus the Jets on Oct. 4, but his limited showing in that session seemingly won't be enough to clear him to suit up Sunday. The Bears have a Week 10 bye on tap, so it comes as no surprise that the team likely will hold off on Monangai's return for two more weeks. Yet again, D'Andre Swift will pace Chicago's backfield this weekend, with Roschon Johnson also on hand for RB reps.
injuryReports.injury: Toe

injuryReports.name: Salvon Ahmed
injuryReports.returnComment: Ahmed is set to be elevated for the first time since signing with Chicago's practice squad in September. With Zavier Scott (wrist) being placed on injured reserve Thursday and Kyle Monangai dealing with thumb and toe injuries, Ahmed could be called upon to provide additional depth behind D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson against Tampa Bay.
injuryReports.injury: The Bears elevated Ahmed from their practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: Grady Jarrett
injuryReports.returnComment: After missing the Bears' walk-through practice Wednesday, Jarrett logged a limited practice Thursday and then upgraded again to a full practice Friday. He should start on the interior of the defensive line next to Jeffery Simmons again in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Jarrett (groin) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: Zavier Scott
injuryReports.returnComment: Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Wrist

injuryReports.name: Kentavius Street
injuryReports.returnComment: Street was injured in Monday night's win over the Seahawks and had to be carted to the locker room. He's now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Fellow DT Grady Jarrett (groin) was also injured in Seattle, making the move for Jeffery Simmons that much more important for Chicago.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Braxton Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones underwent right knee surgery Tuesday, and as a result, he will be forced to miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign. In his absence, Theo Benedet (shoulder) will continue to operate as the team's primary option at left tackle.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Stephen Carlson
injuryReports.returnComment: When Cole Kmet went to the Bears' injured reserve list with a season-ending knee injury following Week 7, it left the team with just two healthy tight ends on its active roster, so the move gives the club some much-needed depth at the position. As long as starter Colston Loveland and rookie third-rounder Sam Roush remain available, though, Carlson's role will likely be limited as the season progresses.
injuryReports.injury: Chicago signed Carlson from its practice squad to its 53-man roster Wednesday, Brendan Sugrue of USA Today reports.

injuryReports.name: Sam Roush
injuryReports.returnComment: With Cole Kmet landing on injured reserve with a season-ending knee injury, Roush stepped into an increased role on offense, as his 53 percent snap share represented a season-best mark. However, the added playing time didn't translate to any involvement in the passing game, as Roush ran just 12 routes on the night. The Bears' frequent usage of two-tight-end formations should continue to prop up Roush's snap counts, but he's likely to be utilized mainly as a blocker when he's on the field.
injuryReports.injury: Roush went without a target while playing 37 of the Bears' 70 snaps on offense in Monday's 34-17 win over the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Roschon Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: With Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) inactive for a fourth straight game, Johnson continued to serve as the No. 2 running back behind D'Andre Swift. Unsurprisingly, Swift (27 carries for 69 yards and three touchdowns) handled the brunt of the work out of the backfield, with Johnson taking the field for just 14 of the team's 70 offensive snaps. If Monangai is able to make it back for Sunday's matchup with the Buccaneers, Johnson's playing time on offense could disappear entirely.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson carried five times for 17 yards and added an 11-yard reception on his lone target in Monday's 34-17 win over the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Cairo Santos
injuryReports.returnComment: Santos made 44- and 38-yard field goals in the second quarter. It was a nice bounce-back game for the veteran kicker after he'd missed a field-goal try in each of the previous three games. For the season, Santos is 13-for-17 on FGAs and a perfect 25-for-25 on PATs. Being attached to the Bears offense makes Santos an attractive fantasy kicker.
injuryReports.injury: Santos made both field-goal tries and all four PATs in Monday night's 34-17 win over the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Caleb Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams helped set the tone for the Bears' statement road victory by leading a 17-play, 80-yard march that absorbed 8:32 of the first quarter, one that the third-year signal-caller capped off with a one-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden. Williams then managed the game effectively from that point forward, avoiding mistakes while leaning on a workhorse performance from D'Andre Swift (27 carries, three touchdowns) and an often dominating effort from his defense. Williams now has a three-game streak of interception-free performances and is up to 1,267 passing yards through five contests heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Williams completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions and rushed twice for one yard in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Kalif Raymond
injuryReports.returnComment: Raymond's most memorable contribution was a 39-yard dash on a third-down play early in the fourth quarter to take the ball down to Seattle's five-yard line and set up a D'Andre Swift touchdown. Though he didn't put up massive numbers, Raymond's 53 total yards were his most since Week 3 and represented more yardage than he had recorded over his previous four games combined. Raymond remains a shaky fantasy play given his recent numbers, and a Week 9 matchup against a Tampa Bay defense that has been pretty stingy on wideouts doesn't improve his outlook.
injuryReports.injury: Raymond finished Monday's 34-17 win against Seattle with two catches for 14 yards on three targets along with one rush for 39 yards.

injuryReports.name: Rome Odunze
injuryReports.returnComment: Odunze led the Bears in receiving yards on the night while finishing second in receptions and targets. The third-year wideout's catch and yardage totals both qualified as his second highest of the season, and Odunze now has 156 receiving yards over the last pair of contests for his most productive two-game stretch this season. Odunze is averaging a career-best 16.7 yards per catch and already has a career-high 14 receptions of 20-plus yards heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Odunze brought in four of six targets for 87 yards in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Luther Burden III
injuryReports.returnComment: Burden tied Colston Loveland for the team lead in both receptions and targets, and he was on the receiving end of Caleb Williams' one touchdown pass of the night. The second-year wideout's scoring grab came from one yard out in the first quarter and was his third of the season, and Burden now has a 19-281-2 line on 21 targets over the last three games heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Burden secured seven of nine targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Colston Loveland
injuryReports.returnComment: Loveland continued his upward trajectory by tying Luther Burden for the team lead in catches and targets, and he finished second in receiving yards to Rome Odunze. The second-year tight end's fourth-quarter fumble was costly for the moment, however, as Loveland lost the ball at the Bears' 21-yard line following an eight-yard reception, and the turnover ultimately led to the Seahawks' final touchdown of the contest. Nevertheless, Loveland now has at least six receptions in four of the last five games, including three straight, and he's drawn 21 targets over the last pair of contests alone heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Loveland secured seven of nine targets for 65 yards and lost a fumble in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: D'Andre Swift
injuryReports.returnComment: Swift put in a full night's work while repeatedly butting heads with the Seahawks' elite run defense, as his longest run went for only seven yards, and he averaged 2.6 yards per carry overall. He sealed the win for Chicago with his third touchdown of the game, a five-yard run with 4:41 remaining. That score was preceded by one- and five-yard TDs earlier in the second half, and Swift's carry total was a season high. The veteran running back is up to a career-high 10 rushing touchdowns heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Swift rushed 27 times for 69 yards and three touchdowns and brought in two of three targets for 10 yards in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Case Keenum
injuryReports.returnComment: Keenum will serve as the No. 3 QB for the third straight week, while Tyson Bagent slots in as the primary backup behind starter Caleb Williams. Keenum will only be eligible to enter the contest if both Williams and Bagent are forced out of the game.
injuryReports.injury: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive but will operate as the Bears' emergency third quarterback for Monday night's matchup against the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Jack Sanborn
injuryReports.returnComment: Sanborn was unable to play against the Patriots in Week 7 due to a concussion, but he was a full participant in all three practices of Week 8 prep, and he has cleared the league's protocol after passing an evaluation from an independent neurologist. He has four tackles (three solo) across six regular-season games while serving mostly on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Sanborn (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Taylen Green
injuryReports.returnComment: With Deshaun Watson (concussion) inactive, Green will stay the emergency third option for a different starter-backup duo. Shedeur Sanders is set to start at quarterback, with Dillon Gabriel ready to back him up. Green will only enter the contest if both Sanders and Gabriel exit due to injury, illness or ejection.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Deshaun Watson
injuryReports.returnComment: Watson, who reported concussion symptoms Tuesday, didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday before being deemed limited Friday and subsequently heading into the weekend with a 'questionable' tag. Though Watson has cleared the NFL's concussion protocol, the Browns have elected to err on the side of caution with the QB who has compiled a 5-3 record as the team's starter to date. With Watson listed as inactive versus New Orleans, Shedeur Sanders will draw the start, while Dillon Gabriel will serve as Cleveland's No. 2 signal caller. Taylen Green is the team's emergency No. 3 QB.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Noah Igbinoghene
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Justin Jefferson
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Parker Brailsford
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Maliek Collins
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Elbow

injuryReports.name: Dillon Gabriel
injuryReports.returnComment: It was announced earlier in the week that Shedeur Sanders would start Sunday's contest due to Deshaun Watson being in concussion protocol, and although Watson has not officially been ruled out for Week 9 as of yet, he reportedly will be. That will leave the backup spot to Gabriel, but presumably for only one contest, as the report notes Watson is expected back for Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Gabriel "will serve as the backup quarterback" Sunday against the Saints, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Carsen Ryan
injuryReports.returnComment: Ryan was signed to the practice squad and then elevated in anticipation of Sunday's contest. The tight end has played in all but one game for the Browns and will continue in his role as the No. 3 tight end, a role that will see him predominantly utilized on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: The Browns elevated Ryan from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Quincy Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams finished the week with back-to-back limited practices heading into Week 9 against the Saints. Williams has recorded 55 total tackles (32 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and four forced fumbles in eight games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Williams has no injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.

injuryReports.name: Denzel Boston
injuryReports.returnComment: With Boston upgrading from limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday to full participation Friday, he should be fine for his usual role as a near-every-down player in a young Cleveland offense. It'll be his first chance to work with Shedeur Sanders extensively outside of a practice environment, as the Browns reportedly won't start Deshaun Watson (head) even if he clears concussion protocol before the game.
injuryReports.injury: Boston (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at New Orleans, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.

injuryReports.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Coach Todd Monken said Fannin is "a little sore" but will be out there against New Orleans. On paper, it's a great spot for Fannin, but playing at less than 100 percent knocks him down a peg as a backend TE1 for fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Fannin (groin) will play Sunday against the Saints, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Shedeur Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: Coach Todd Monken said the move is because Deshaun Watson (concussion) missed so much practice time this week. Watson has been one of the worst statistical quarterbacks in the league over the last month, so Sanders could potentially keep the job if he has a good game versus the Saints. Sanders' insertion under center doesn't change the outlook of the offense, as both Watson and Sanders are game-manager types.
injuryReports.injury: Sanders will start at quarterback Sunday against the Saints, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.

injuryReports.name: Andre Szmyt
injuryReports.returnComment: Szmyt converted his 31-yard and 32-yard field-goal attempts in the second quarter of Sunday's contest. The kicker accounted for all six of the Browns' points in the divisional loss. Szmyt is now 16-for-18 on field-goal attempts and 11-for-12 on PATs through eight regular-season games in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Szmyt made both of his field-goal attempts in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jerry Jeudy
injuryReports.returnComment: Quarterback Deshaun Watson had a relatively productive day with 324 passing yards (albeit without a score), but Jeudy was on the receiving end of only one of his passes. The veteran wideout logged his usual amount of playing time, notching a 60 percent offensive snap share to finish third among Cleveland wide receivers. It was the third time this season Jeudy has finished without a catch, but the other two instances were in Weeks 3 and 4, and he had been more involved of late, averaging 3.5 catches and 36.3 receiving yards over his previous four games. With that in mind, he could get back on track in Week 9 against a New Orleans defense that has been middle-of-the-pack against wideouts this year.
injuryReports.injury: Jeudy did not catch his lone target Sunday in Cleveland's 27-6 loss to Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Malachi Corley
injuryReports.returnComment: For the fourth time in eight appearances, Corley logged double-digit snaps on offense, but the third-year receiver has yet to draw a target this season. He'll continue to provide most of his value to the Browns as a kickoff returner.
injuryReports.injury: Corley went untargeted while playing 13 of 70 snaps on offense Sunday in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers. He returned one kickoff for 26 yards.

injuryReports.name: Tylan Wallace
injuryReports.returnComment: The reception was Wallace's second of the season, after he previously notched a 12-yard grab in a Week 6 win over the Ravens. A key part of the Browns' special-teams coverage units, Wallace continues to handle a limited role on offense while the the team relies primarily on rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston and veteran Jerry Jeudy to fill out snaps at receiver.
injuryReports.injury: Wallace recorded a three-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Bond
injuryReports.returnComment: Since posting a 3-74-0 receiving line on seven targets in a Week 5 loss to the Jets, Bond has settled back into a muted role on offense. He's logged single-digit snaps in three straight contests, going without a target in each of those games.
injuryReports.injury: Bond went without a target while taking the field for eight of the Browns' 70 snaps on offense in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers. He returned one kickoff for 26 yards.

injuryReports.name: Dylan Sampson
injuryReports.returnComment: Sampson was out-carried 11 to one by Quinshon Judkins, but the former has carved out a role as the preferred pass-catching back for Cleveland since returning from injured reserve in Week 7. Over the last two games, Sampson has turned 11 targets into nine catches for 94 yards while adding seven carries for 52 yards. Sampson will have some PPR fantasy appeal during weeks when the Browns are projected to trail on the scoreboard.
injuryReports.injury: Sampson rushed one time for seven yards and caught six of eight targets for 62 yards in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: KC Concepcion
injuryReports.returnComment: After a breakout game last Sunday against the Titans, which saw Concepcion record eight grabs for 129 yards on 10 targets, the rookie wideout came crashing back down against a divisional foe. Concepcion's four targets were a distant fourth on the team behind Harold Fannin (12), Denzel Boston (11) and Dylan Sampson (eight), and his four looks were good for just a 10.3 percent target share. Concepcion will try to rebound next Sunday against the Saints, but he's shown little upside, with zero touchdowns and just two games with more than 50 receiving yards.
injuryReports.injury: Concepcion caught three of four targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Joey Porter Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Porter began Week 9 prep with a full practice session, but he was limited both Thursday and Friday due to the ankle issue. The star cornerback is now set to miss his fifth game of the campaign. Cobie Durant is a prime candidate to start in Porter's place Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: DeMarvion Overshown
injuryReports.returnComment: Overshown wasn't able to overcome injuries to his hamstring and back in time to be ready to suit up Sunday. He was limited in practice both Thursday and Friday, so the issues may not cause a long-term absence. Shemar James is likely to start alongside Dee Winters at inside linebacker for the Cowboys on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Luke Schoonmaker
injuryReports.returnComment: Schoonmaker continues to tend to a groin issue and will miss his second straight game. He did manage a trio of limited practices during the week, so the tight end may be able to play next Sunday, Nov. 15, against San Francisco. Dallas' tight-end corps will consist of Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: KaVontae Turpin
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Ribs

injuryReports.name: Tyrus Wheat
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Ajani Cornelius
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Jake Ferguson
injuryReports.returnComment: Ferguson left last Sunday's loss to the Cardinals on the Cowboys' first possession and wasn't able to return due to an ankle injury. He was diagnosed with a low-ankle sprain, and while head coach Brian Schottenheimer relayed to Jon Machota of The Athletic on Monday that Ferguson has a chance to play in Week 9, the tight end managed just one limited practice (Friday) and was listed as questionable. Now that Ferguson is confirmed to be active, his workload is unclear with two other TEs (Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell) also available to the offense.
injuryReports.injury: Ferguson (ankle) is listed as active Sunday in Indianapolis.

injuryReports.name: George Pickens
injuryReports.returnComment: For a second week in a row, Pickens endured practice restrictions due to a hamstring injury, leaving him questionable to suit up in Week 9. On Friday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer told Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site that he's "hopeful" Pickens will be available this weekend, but that didn't come to pass. With Pickens and fellow WR KaVontae Turpin (ribs) inactive Sunday, CeeDee Lamb, Ryan Flournoy, Jonathan Mingo, Camden Brown and Jordan Hudson will compose Dallas' receiving corps.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Jonathan Bullard
injuryReports.returnComment: Bullard had his practice window opened Oct. 29 and was a full participant in all three of the Cowboys' practices this week. However, he's not yet ready to return to game action. Bullard's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against San Francisco.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Marist Liufau
injuryReports.returnComment: Liufau has yet to play this season after breaking his left forearm in Dallas' preseason finale against New Orleans. He was designated to return Oct. 22 and was a full participant in all three practices this week. That bodes well for his chance of playing Sunday, which could be especially helpful to the Cowboys' pass rush after Malachi Lawrence (ankle) landed on IR on Saturday.
injuryReports.injury: Liufau (forearm) was activated from injured reserve Saturday and is questionable for Sunday's contest versus the Colts, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Hudson
injuryReports.returnComment: Hudson will make his NFL debut if he gets into Sunday's game against the Colts. The SMU product latched on with the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent in May. Hudson is unlikely to see much action versus Indianapolis, and whether he logs any offensive snaps at all could depend upon whether fellow wideout George Pickens (questionable, hamstring) is able to play.
injuryReports.injury: The Cowboys elevated Hudson from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: James Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: Mitchell was elevated for the second straight week ahead of Sunday's matchup against Indianapolis. In his 2026 debut last Sunday versus Arizona, the tight end logged a healthy 31 offensive snaps but didn't log a target or touch. How much Mitchell plays in Indianapolis will likely depend on whether Jake Ferguson (ankle) and Luke Schoonmaker (groin) are able to suit up.
injuryReports.injury: The Cowboys elevated Mitchell from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Malachi Lawrence
injuryReports.returnComment: Lawrence suffered an ankle injury last Sunday in a loss to Arizona and had already been ruled out for Week 9. The move to IR means he'll need to miss at least three additional games, so the earliest Lawrence can return is Monday, Dec. 7, against Seattle. The Cowboys activated fellow linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) from IR on Saturday to fill Lawrence's roster spot.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Tyler Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited in consecutive sessions to start Week 9 prep. The star left guard is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest to defend Dak Prescott against the Colts' pass rush.
injuryReports.injury: Smith (ankle) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: P.J. Locke
injuryReports.returnComment: Locke has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest. The starting strong safety has played in just three regular-season games so far in 2026, with he logged only three defensive snaps played in Week 2. However he seems to be getting healthy and should therefore be set for a prominent role moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: Locke (concussion) holds no injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Caleb Downs
injuryReports.returnComment: Downs upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice, clearing the league's concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts. The rookie first-rounder is all set to suit up for the contest as the starting slot cornerback and reserve punt returner for the Cowboys.
injuryReports.injury: Downs (concussion) has no injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Dee Winters
injuryReports.returnComment: Winters was limited Wednesday. However, after logging a full session Thursday, all signs are pointing toward his availability for the Week 9 meeting with the Colts. The 2023 No. 216 overall pick has appeared in six games in his first season in Dallas, amassing 35 total tackles (23 solo) and one interception.
injuryReports.injury: Winters (calf) was a full participant in practice Thursday, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Drew Shelton
injuryReports.returnComment: The fourth-round rookie has been sidelined since Week 4 and has played a total of five offensive snaps this season.
injuryReports.injury: Shelton (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Thompson
injuryReports.returnComment: Thompson is still working his way back from a hamstring injury that forced the team to place him on injured reserve in late September, and he is not ready to return to practice quite yet. In his absence, P.J. Locke (concussion), Malik Hooker and Markquese Bell are poised to continue to operate as the Cowboys' primary safeties.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Tyler Goodson
injuryReports.returnComment: Dallas wasn't really able to get anything going on the ground in Week 8, totaling just 93 rushing yards on 39 carries. Just like the offense as a whole, Goodson found a bit more success in the passing game, and he posted his best receiving total since back in 2024. As long as starter Javonte Williams remains available, though, Goodson should stay in a change-of-pace role.
injuryReports.injury: Goodson took seven carries for 14 yards and caught both of his two targets for 19 yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss versus the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Brevyn Spann-Ford
injuryReports.returnComment: Starting tight end Jake Ferguson logged only four offensive snaps before leaving Sunday's contest with an ankle injury, and Spann-Ford ended up playing a career-high 65 offensive snaps as a result. He ended up second on the team in targets behind CeeDee Lamb (11), and he could be worth a look as a streaming option in deeper formats if Ferguson is unable to suit up in Week 9 at Indianapolis.
injuryReports.injury: Spann-Ford caught four of five targets for 31 yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss versus the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Brandon Aubrey
injuryReports.returnComment: Aubrey missed a 61-yard field goal before halftime in a game that ended with a three-point difference. The kicker converted from 31 yards, 35 yards and 41 yards in the contest as the Cowboys offense ended up stalling after long drives multiple times. Aubrey moves to 15-for-19 on field-goal attempts and 20-for-21 on PATs through eight regular-season games in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Aubrey made three of his four field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Cowboys' 33-30 overtime loss to the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Ryan Flournoy
injuryReports.returnComment: Flournoy ran 26 routes on Dak Prescott's 38 dropbacks against Arizona, and with Dallas moving more toward three-wide sets and away from multiple tight-end sets while decreasing Jake Ferguson's (ankle) playing time, Flournoy has been a big beneficiary in recent weeks. Over the last four weeks, Flournoy has recorded 238 yards and two touchdowns on 18 grabs across 21 targets. He's achieved WR4 valuation in fantasy and would receive a major boost if CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens ever went down with an injury.
injuryReports.injury: Flournoy caught three of four targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Dak Prescott
injuryReports.returnComment: Arizona's defense had been plenty exploitable this season, allowing 243.7 yards per game and 17 TDs through the air to opposing QBs heading into Week 8 action. Even with his main skill-position talents available Sunday, though, Prescott didn't crack 200 passing yards for the first time since Week 1. He salvaged his day with his first TD on the ground of the campaign, which supplemented a nine-yard TD connection with WR Ryan Flournoy. Prescott and the Cowboys offense will look to get back on track next Sunday versus an exploitable Colts defense on the road.
injuryReports.injury: Prescott was 19-for-29 passing for 195 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions while rushing seven times for 20 yards and one more TD during Sunday's 33-30 overtime defeat to the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Dondrea Tillman
injuryReports.returnComment: Tillman was on the injury report ahead of the Week 9 meeting with Carolina due to a hamstring issue. However, he will avoid his second absence of the 2026 campaign. The 28-year-old has appeared in seven games for the Broncos this season, amassing 19 total tackles (10 solo).
injuryReports.injury: Tillman is active for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Lil'Jordan Humphrey
injuryReports.returnComment: Humphrey has appeared in Denver's last four regular-season contests. However, he will be a healthy scratch for the meeting with Carolina, meaning his next opportunity to play will come in Week 11 against the Raiders, following the Broncos' bye.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Talanoa Hufanga
injuryReports.returnComment: Hufanga was considered a game-time call for this one. However, he won't suit up for a fourth consecutive contest. Hufanga is seemingly moving in the right direction, so there's a chance he will be back on the field in Week 11, following the Broncos' bye.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Pat Bryant
injuryReports.returnComment: The second-year wideout foreshadowed a return to game action this past week by putting in three full practices, which led to his activation from injured reserve Saturday. Bryant still carried a questionable tag heading into Sunday, but with his availability now confirmed, he should be ready to reprise the No. 3 role he filled behind Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle prior to his Week 4 injury. Bryant saw generally modest volume during his three-plus games to date, posting a 9-133-1 line on 12 targets and adding a 16-yard rush on his one carry.
injuryReports.injury: Bryant (ankle) is active for Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Sam Ehlinger
injuryReports.returnComment: Ehlinger is officially inactive Sunday, though he will be available if Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Brandon Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Kris Abrams-Draine
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Dallen Bentley
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Kage Casey
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Eyioma Uwazurike
injuryReports.returnComment: Uwazurike wasn't able to practice at all this week due to a shoulder issue. He started seven of Denver's first eight games, but he's now required to miss the team's next four contests. Third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim could see the first gameday action of his career as a result.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Cody Schrader
injuryReports.returnComment: Schrader has been elevated for the second straight week after making his Broncos debut last Sunday against Kansas City. He logged just two offensive snaps and didn't get a touch or target in that game, but he he did rack up 50 yards on two kick returns. Schrader figures to fill a similar role against the Panthers as the No. 3 RB behind Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins.
injuryReports.injury: The Broncos elevated Schrader from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's matchup in Carolina, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Alex Singleton
injuryReports.returnComment: Singleton continued to rack up a vast number of stops -- it was the fifth time this season he's recorded double-digit tackles. The star linebacker also registered a sack for the second straight week, coming up huge when he brought down Patrick Mahomes for a six-yard loss late in the fourth quarter on third down. The next play was a missed Harrison Butker 54-yard field-goal try, which led to Denver pulling off the comeback with a touchdown less than a minute later. Singleton has been an elite IDP asset in fantasy this season, as he leads the NFL by a wide margin with 101 tackles through eight weeks.
injuryReports.injury: Singleton notched 14 tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, and defensed a pass in Sunday's 28-24 victory against the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Evan Engram
injuryReports.returnComment: Bo Nix targeted 10 different pass catchers on 32 total pass attempts, and it was rookie RB Jonah Coleman who led the team in receiving with a 4-63-0 line on five targets. Engram has just three catches for 15 yards over his last three games and isn't a recommended fantasy bet ahead of Sunday's date with the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: Engram failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 28-24 win over the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Wil Lutz
injuryReports.returnComment: Lutz's field-goal tries were good from 39 and 45 yards in the first half. Kicking in Denver's anemic offense through eight games, the veteran has made just 14 of 17 FGAs and all 14 PATs. He's not an exciting fantasy kicker despite playing his home games in a kicker-friendly environment.
injuryReports.injury: Lutz made both field-goal attempts and both PATs in Sunday's 28-24 win over the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Nate Adkins
injuryReports.returnComment: The block-first tight end secured a two-yard score in the fourth quarter to pull the Broncos within three points, before they scored the eventual game-winning touchdown on the next possession. Adkins now has six grabs for 44 yards and a score on seven targets this season. He has no fantasy appeal.
injuryReports.injury: Adkins caught both of his targets for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 win over the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Waddle
injuryReports.returnComment: Despite the fact that the wideout was playing through a chest injury, Waddle came up big when it counted, connecting with Bo Nix on a one-yard TD in the second quarter before snagging a two-point conversion in the fourth as Denver mounted a comeback from a 24-13 deficit. Waddle's 29-315-2 line on 51 targets through his first eight games as a Bronco is disappointing, but he still has time to pick up the pace beginning with a Week 9 tilt against the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: Waddle caught three of six targets for 39 yards and a touchdown and added a two-point conversion in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.

injuryReports.name: J.K. Dobbins
injuryReports.returnComment: While the veteran RB got the start, by the end of the game Dobbins had fully given way to rookie Jonah Coleman, who wound up delivering 104 scrimmage yards on 15 touches and scored the game-winning touchdown. With RJ Harvey (knee) on IR, Dobbins will still have a role in the Denver backfield, but Coleman made a compelling case Sunday to become the team's new No. 1 back. Dobbins should at least be more productive in Week 9, even on limited volume, against a Panthers defense that's among the worst in the league against the run.
injuryReports.injury: Dobbins carried the ball seven times for 13 yards in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.

injuryReports.name: Jonah Coleman
injuryReports.returnComment: With RJ Harvey (knee) on the shelf, Coleman saw a season-high 15 touches compared to J.K. Dobbins' seven, and the rookie was instrumental in the Broncos' fourth-quarter comeback. After a Harrison Butker missed field goal gave Denver great field position, Coleman was a one-man show on a two-play drive, taking a short pass from Bo Nix and turning it into a 51-yard gain before punching in a five-yard TD on the other side of the two-minute warning. Dobbins will still mix in on early downs, but Coleman may have just seized control of the backfield for the Broncos. He'll look to solidify his spot in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that's among the worst in the league against the run.
injuryReports.injury: Coleman carried the ball 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown and caught four of five targets for 63 yards in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.

injuryReports.name: Bo Nix
injuryReports.returnComment: The Broncos were staring at a 24-13 deficit heading into the fourth quarter, but late comebacks are nothing new for Nix. The QB hit Nate Adkins for a two-yard score with about nine minutes left before connecting with Jonah Coleman on a 51-yard catch-and-run to set up the game-winning TD plunge by the rookie RB just after the two-minute warning. It's the 15th time that Nix has led Denver on a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime, the most by any quarterback in the first three seasons of his career since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970. While he's thrown multiple TDs just twice in the first eight games of the season, Nix has gone five straight contests without tossing an INT. He'll take a 9:3 TD:INT into a Week 9 road tilt against the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: Nix completed 20 of 32 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City. He added four rushing yards on three carries and threw a two-point conversion to Jaylen Waddle.

injuryReports.name: Courtland Sutton
injuryReports.returnComment: Sutton went to the medical tent after taking a hard hit, but the wideout was able to return to action not long after he did so. In the process he'll bolster a Denver Week 9 WR corps that also includes Jaylen Waddle, Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims and Lil'Jordan Humphrey.
injuryReports.injury: Sutton (undisclosed) briefly left Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Zach Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen injured his hamstring in Week 7 against the Cardinals, but he's been given the green light to play Sunday after having his reps limited during Week 8 prep. He has 24 tackles (10 solo), including 4.5 sacks, two pass defenses and one forced fumble through seven regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Allen (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jacob Saylors
injuryReports.returnComment: Saylors carried a questionable designation heading into this contest, though he won't be on the field in Week 9, marking his first absence of the 2026 campaign. With Sione Vaki (ankle) available, Saylors likely wouldn't have been very involved, regardless.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Sione Vaki
injuryReports.returnComment: Vaki didn't practice Friday, resulting in a questionable tag for Week 9. However, he will be out there against the Dolphins and may continue to be more involved after totaling 11 carries in the Week 8 win over the Vikings.
injuryReports.injury: Vaki (ankle) is available for Sunday's game against Miami.

injuryReports.name: Mekhi Wingo
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: DJ Wonnum
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Cade Mays
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jackson Meeks
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: D.J. Reed
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Hip

injuryReports.name: Ahmed Hassanein
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: St. Brown tended to a rib injury during Week 9 prep that limited him in all three sessions and left him questionable ahead of the weekend. Having said that, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported Sunday morning that St. Brown is expected to play, which now has been confirmed. St. Brown will be taking on a Dolphins defense that has allowed an NFL-worst 9.8 yards per target to opposing wide receivers this season.
injuryReports.injury: St. Brown (ribs) is active for Sunday's game in Miami.

injuryReports.name: Jabari Small
injuryReports.returnComment: Small signed with the team's practice squad in September and is now set to be elevated for the first time this season. With Sione Vaki (ankle) and Jacob Saylors (neck) both dealing with injuries, Small could be in line to serve as Detroit's No. 2 running back behind Jahmyr Gibbs against Miami.
injuryReports.injury: The Lions elevated Small from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's matchup versus the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Jack Campbell
injuryReports.returnComment: Campbell suffered a neck injury while making a tackle in the third quarter of last Sunday's win over Minnesota and remains in the hospital. Detroit head coach Dan Campbell shared Friday that the linebacker continues to improve, but  his placement on IR means he'll miss at least the team's next four games. K.J. Britt, who Detroit signed off New England's practice squad Wednesday, may be asked to immediately step into a starting role.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Kerby Joseph
injuryReports.returnComment: Joseph was a limited participant throughout Week 9 prep. Despite maintaining consistent practice participation, the free safety will not be activated from the reserve/PUP list for Sunday's game. The Lions will likely wait until Joseph has logged multiple full sessions and is fully ready to return to the field. Chuck Clark will continue to start at free safety opposite Brian Branch.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Brian Branch
injuryReports.returnComment: With consecutive full practices to close out Week 9 prep, Branch has officially cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol. The starting strong safety is all set to suit up for Sunday's game alongside free safety Chuck Clark.
injuryReports.injury: Branch (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Jimmy Rolder
injuryReports.returnComment: This move was anticipated, as Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in the Lions' win over Minnesota on Sunday. The rookie linebacker logged a career-high 17 defensive snaps and notched his first NFL sack in that contest, so his injury comes at an unfortunate time. Rolder will now turn his focus toward rehabbing the injury in order to be ready for offseason activities in 2027.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring
