injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Travis Kelce
injuryReports.returnComment: Kelce was deemed a limited participant Wednesday, but the tight end's full participation Thursday paves the way for him to be in uniform Sunday against the Jets. Over his last two games, the Chiefs' leader in catches and receiving yards has amassed nine catches (on 15 targets) for 111 yards with a TD, and as long as he stays healthy he'll merit weekly fantasy lineup consideration.
injuryReports.injury: Kelce (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Rashee Rice
injuryReports.returnComment: Rice is off the injury report Thursday after kicking off Week 9 prep with a limited session Wednesday. The oft-injured wide receiver has been limited to five appearances this season, one of which he left before recording a catch, but he has 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns across the other four games. With Rice getting healthier, he could feast Sunday against a Jets defense that's allowing 30.7 points per game during an active three-game losing streak.
injuryReports.injury: Rice (hamstring/knee) practiced without limitations Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Harrison Butker
injuryReports.returnComment: Butker -- who has made 12 of his 18 field-goal attempts in seven games this season -- converted one of his two tries along with with all three point-after attempts in the Chiefs' Week 8 loss to the Broncos. Despite his recent accuracy issues, Butker will retain his kicking role this weekend, even though the Chiefs recently signed Justin Tucker to the practice squad.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Andy Reid said that Butker will remain the Chiefs' kicker for Sunday's game against the Jets, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Cyrus Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie wide receiver usurped Jalen Royals on the depth chart, operating as the clear WR3 behind Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy. Allen ran 22 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 44 dropbacks, but with both Rice and Worthy healthy alongside Travis Kelce and Kenneth Walker, there doesn't appear to be much juice to squeeze for Allen.
injuryReports.injury: Allen caught two of three targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Noah Gray
injuryReports.returnComment: The Chiefs' TE2 caught a four-yard score in the third quarter, his first touchdown of the season. Kansas City uses plenty of 12 personnel, deploying both Travis Kelce and Gray on offense, but Gray handles more of the blocking duties. On the season, he has 14 grabs for 173 yards and a touchdown. There isn't much meat on the bone here for fantasy purposes.
injuryReports.injury: Gray caught both of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Emmett Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie running back flashed his explosiveness on a 73-yard catch-and-run in the second quarter that produced Johnson's first career NFL touchdown. He came into Sunday with a 9-109-0 line on 11 targets through six games, and his six touches were firmly behind Kenneth Walker's 25, but Johnson's breakout performance can only encourage Andy Reid to find more ways to get the ball in his hands. Johnson will look to build on this effort in Week 9 against the Jets.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson carried the ball once for 15 yards and caught all five of his targets for 128 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos. He added 44 yards on his only kickoff return.

injuryReports.name: Xavier Worthy
injuryReports.returnComment: Worthy put together another disappointing performance, reeling in three passes while failing to exceed 15 receiving yards for the second straight game. The wide receiver operated in a more prominent role for a couple weeks with Rashee Rice sidelined with a hamstring injury, but Rice returned to action Sunday and caught seven of eight targets for 53 yards. Worthy will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup with the Jets.
injuryReports.injury: Worthy caught three of six targets for 13 yards during Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Kenneth Walker III
injuryReports.returnComment: The star running back was held below 100 scrimmage yards for a second straight game, but Walker watched his rookie backup, Emmett Johnson, erupt for a 5-128-1 line on five targets and take his only carry for 15 yards. Walker is still the clear No. 1 in the Kansas City backfield, but Johnson may have earned more consistent work with Sunday's impressive effort -- touches which might come at Walker's expense. He'll head into a Week 9 meeting with the Jets second in the race for the NFL rushing crown with 770 yards, just behind Bijan Robinson's 780.
injuryReports.injury: Walker carried the ball 21 times for 69 yards and caught four of five targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Patrick Mahomes
injuryReports.returnComment: The two-time MVP threw a TD in each of the first three quarters, including a four-yard toss to Noah Gray in the third that gave Kansas City a 24-13 lead, but Mahomes got shut out of the end zone over the final 15 minutes as Denver staged a comeback. It was the second three-touchdown performance of the season for Mahomes as well as his second 300-yard effort, after he threw for 382 yards and three scores against the Colts in Week 2. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 9 against a Jets defense that's allowed three straight quarterbacks to produce at least three TDs against it.
injuryReports.injury: Mahomes completed 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos. He added six rushing yards on two carries.

injuryReports.name: L'Jarius Sneed
injuryReports.returnComment: Sneed was initially given the questionable tag for Sunday's game against the Broncos. He's been able to play through a lingering knee issue, but his placement on IR indicates that the injury has gotten to the point that an extended absence is warranted for the seventh-year defensive back. Sneed will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Bills on Thursday, Nov. 26. Jaden Hicks, Jadon Canady, Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace are all candidates to see more work in the secondary due to the absences of both Sneed and Mansoor Delane (shoulder) for Sunday's AFC West tilt.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jaylon Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: The lack of an injury designation indicates that Moore has cleared the league's concussion protocol. He should reclaim his starting spot at right tackle while Joshua Ezeudu reverts to a depth role.
injuryReports.injury: Moore (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Omarr Norman-Lott
injuryReports.returnComment: Norman-Lott was limited in his return to practice Wednesday. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025. The Chiefs now have 21 days to activate Norman-Lott from the PUP list, otherwise he would be forced to miss the entire 2026 season.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - ACL

injuryReports.name: Chamarri Conner
injuryReports.returnComment: Conner was on the field for every single defensive snap for a second consecutive game following the Chiefs' Week 5 bye. He missed the first three games of the regular season due to a knee injury but has suited up for each of the team's last three contests, during which he has accumulated 17 tackles (nine solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense.
injuryReports.injury: Conner finished Sunday's 20-3 loss to Seattle with seven tackles (two solo).

injuryReports.name: Nohl Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: The second-year defensive back's 10 tackles were a career best, and his interception off Sam Darnold late in the second quarter was also the first of Williams' NFL career. Williams is up to 29 tackles (17 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and seven pass defenses (including one interception) through six regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Williams finished Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks with 10 tackles (four solo) and one interception.

injuryReports.name: Nick Bolton
injuryReports.returnComment: Bolton played all but one of the Chiefs' 69 defensive snaps during Sunday's loss, and he finished second on the team in tackles behind Drue Tranquill (12). Bolton has recorded double-digit stops in four of six regular-season games and is up to 59 tackles (29 solo) and two pass defenses on the year.
injuryReports.injury: Bolton registered 11 tackles (six solo) during the Chiefs' 20-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Drue Tranquill
injuryReports.returnComment: Tranquil led the Chiefs in combined tackles Sunday, and he was one of three Kansas City defenders to reach double-digit stops. He's logged at least seven tackles in each of the first six games of the regular season and is up to 48 tackles (22 solo), two pass defenses and one fumble recovery in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Tranquill finished Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks with 12 tackles (four solo).

injuryReports.name: Thomas Booker IV
injuryReports.returnComment: Booker was limited in practice Wednesday, then sat out the sessions Thursday and Friday entirely. He's thus set to miss his first game of the campaign. Booker typically plays one-third to one-half of Las Vegas' defensive snaps, and Tonka Hemingway may be asked to log a bigger workload with Booker sidelined.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Dont'e Thornton Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Thornton was activated from IR last Tuesday but was a healthy scratch Sunday versus the Jets. He picked up a back injury that resulted in a limited practice Thursday this week, but with a return to full participation Friday, the second-year wideout will be available to face the 49ers. However, it's unclear if he'll suit up Sunday given his healthy scratch last weekend.
injuryReports.injury: Thornton (back) does not have a designation for Sunday's battle against San Francisco, Paul Gutierrez of the Raiders' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Darien Porter
injuryReports.returnComment: Porter continues to deal with the groin injury he suffered early in the first quarter of the Raiders' Week 8 win over the Jets. If the cornerback cannot suit up for Sunday's contest, Jermod McCoy or Hezekiah Masses will likely start at outside cornerback across from Eric Stokes.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Nakobe Dean
injuryReports.returnComment: Dean was able to notch exactly 12 stops for the fourth game in a row and fifth time this season. The linebacker is out to a great start to his first campaign in Las Vegas, registering 80 total tackles (38 solo), including 1.5 sacks, while also adding an interception and three forced fumbles over eight contests so far.
injuryReports.injury: Dean recorded 12 total tackles (two solo) during Sunday's 38-33 victory against the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Jeremy Chinn
injuryReports.returnComment: Chinn had quite a day in Week 8, finishing second on the team in takedowns while also jumping in front of a deep ball from Jets quarterback Geno Smith for the safety's first interception of the year. Chinn has now compiled 56 total tackles (38 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding two forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries and an interception over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Chinn recorded 10 total tackles (four solo) and an interception during Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Cody White
injuryReports.returnComment: White was released by the team Tuesday to make room for Carter Runyon (foot), who was activated off injured reserve. With Runyon now waived and potentially joining the Raiders' practice squad, White was re-signed. To date, the 27-year-old has had the best season of his career, amassing eight catches (19 targets) for 112 yards and three touchdowns.
injuryReports.injury: White was signed by the Raiders on Thursday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Mike Washington Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com, Kubiak said that he "absolutely" believes that Jeanty can be a bell cow running back, but at least for the time being, he looks like he'll be part of a timeshare with Washington. Jeanty has seen his carry count drop or hold steady in each successive game since Week 1, culminating in the 2025 first-round pick logging just two carries in this past Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets, while Washington carried a career-high 25 times for 83 yards. The split in carries may not be quite as dramatic in weeks to come, but Washington appears to have earned himself a sizable piece of the pie while he's averaging 4.3 yards per tote to Jeanty's 3.1 mark through eight games. Jeanty remains the Raiders' clear cut top option on passing downs over Washington, who has recorded just three receptions for 11 yards on six targets so far this season.
injuryReports.injury: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Wednesday that the breakdown in carries between Washington and Ashton Jeanty will be determined on a week-to-week basis, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Ashton Jeanty
injuryReports.returnComment: Jeanty is averaging just 3.1 yards per tote on the season and has seen his carry count gradually decline with each successive game. After rushing a season-high 23 times in a Week 1 win over the Dolphins, Jeanty logged just two carries (for nine yards) in this past Sunday's win over the Jets, while Washington handled 25 carries (for 83 yards). According to McFadden, Kubiak said that he believes Jeanty can "absolutely" be a bell cow running back, but the second-year player out of Boise State looks like he'll be part of a timeshare with Washington until his production on the ground improves. Jeanty is still locked in as the Raiders' clear top back on passing downs, as he ranks first or tied for first with all NFL running backs in targets (49), receptions (37), receiving yards (376) and receiving touchdowns (three).
injuryReports.injury: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Wednesday that the breakdown in carries between Jeanty and Mike Washington will be determined on a week-to-week basis, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Jack Bech
injuryReports.returnComment: Bech returned from a four-game absence due to a forearm injury and logged a 40 percent offensive snap share, but he didn't get any looks from QB Kirk Cousins. In fact, Cousins didn't go to his wideout corps as a whole very often -- 16 of his 26 targets went to tight ends, and another four went to running back Ashton Jeanty. Bech will look to get back into the box score Sunday in a Week 9 matchup in San Francisco.
injuryReports.injury: Bech finished without a target or touch in Sunday's 38-33 Week 8 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Fernando Mendoza
injuryReports.returnComment: With Kirk Cousins helping orchestrate a second-half comeback, Mendoza stayed glued to the sideline for the third straight contest after playing 10 offensive snaps in Week 5 against New England. The Raiders are 4-4 with Cousins playing reasonably well to keep the team in the postseason mix. Mendoza figures to get his shot if/when the Raiders are eliminated from postseason contention.
injuryReports.injury: Mendoza didn't play in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Matt Gay
injuryReports.returnComment: Gay converted a 53-yard field goal with 27 seconds remaining in the contest to put the Raiders up five points. The kicker is now 18-for-20 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 19-for-19 on PATs over eight regular-season games in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Gay converted his sole field-goal attempt and all five PATs in the Raiders' 38-33 win over the Jets on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Tre Tucker
injuryReports.returnComment: Despite quarterback Kirk Cousins throwing for 247 yards, Tucker had only one ball thrown his way. In fact, only one Raiders wideout -- Jalen Nailor -- had a reception, as Cousins targeted tight ends on 16 of his 26 passes. Tucker had caught either four or five passes in each of his prior six games and collected at least 97 receiving yards in three of those contests, though he finished below 45 yards in the other three. It's notable that he logged a season-low 52 percent offensive snap share against the Jets, but he should be in for better days ahead, beginning with a Week 9 matchup in San Francisco.
injuryReports.injury: Tucker did not catch his only target Sunday in the Raiders' 38-33 Week 8 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Michael Mayer
injuryReports.returnComment: Mayer's six targets were second on the team behind Brock Bowers' 10, and only Bowers (26) ran more routes than Mayer's 20 on Kirk Cousins' 27 dropbacks. The tight end has just one touchdown this season but has remained an integral part of Las Vegas' passing attack. He's already surpassed his 2025 catches and yards totals, posting 36 grabs for 351 yards through eight games this season. Mayer will be a fantasy TE2 for next Sunday's date with the 49ers.
injuryReports.injury: Mayer caught five of six targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Nailor
injuryReports.returnComment: Both the catches and yards marked new season highs for Nailor, who entered Sunday with eight grabs for 75 yards and no touchdowns across six games. No team uses its receivers less than the Raiders, and Nailor accounted for four of the five targets between him and Tre Tucker against the Jets. Nailor has minimal fantasy appeal headed into next Sunday's road date with the 49ers.
injuryReports.injury: Nailor caught all four targets for 38 yards in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Kirk Cousins
injuryReports.returnComment: Cousins connected with Brock Bowers for touchdowns of 12 and two yards before scoring on a QB sneak in the third quarter for the 38-year-old QB's first rushing TD of the season and second rushing score since the start of the 2023 regular season. Cousins added a go-ahead two-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Nailor in the fourth quarter to take a 35-30 lead with 11:33 remaining. This was Cousins' fourth three-touchdown passing performance of the season but first since Week 4. All four of those three-TD outings came in Vegas wins, and Cousins has added seven touchdown passes in the Raiders' four losses to bring his TD:INT to 19:5 heading into a Week 9 trip to San Francisco.
injuryReports.injury: Cousins completed 19 of 26 passes for 247 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets. He added five rushing attempts for three yards and a rushing touchdown.

injuryReports.name: Brock Bowers
injuryReports.returnComment: Bowers scored a 12-yard touchdown in the first quarter and added a two-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter. He came just short of a third touchdown later in the third quarter, getting tackled just outside the goal line to set up a one-yard Kirk Cousins rushing TD. Bowers became the first tight end in NFL history to record at least 70 receiving yards in six consecutive appearances to begin a season. He'll try to extend his historic streak in Week 9 against the 49ers while continuing to work as the top target for Kirk Cousins.
injuryReports.injury: Bowers caught seven of 10 targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Rodney Shelley
injuryReports.returnComment: Shelley missed each of Los Angeles' past three games while tending to an ankle injury. However, he followed two limited practices to begin this week with a full session Friday to position himself for a return Sunday. Shelley has played a rotational role in the secondary when active this season while also contributing on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Shelley (ankle) has no designation for Sunday's tilt against the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Denzel Perryman
injuryReports.returnComment: Perryman has been on IR all season due to an undisclosed issue. He was designated to return to practice Wednesday, and the veteran linebacker ended up logging a trio of limited sessions. However, it appears he's not quite ready to return to game action. In order for Perryman to have any chance to play Sunday, he'll need to be activated from IR on Saturday.
injuryReports.injury: Undisclosed

injuryReports.name: Kendall Williamson
injuryReports.returnComment: Willamson didn't practice at all this week, so he presumably picked up the calf injury in last Sunday's loss to the Rams. He's played exclusively on special teams this season, so Williamson's absence shouldn't affect the Chargers' defensive rotations.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Deane Leonard
injuryReports.returnComment: Leonard is presumably still in concussion protocol, though he was able to log limited practice sessions Thursday and Friday. Donte Jackson (hamstring) is returning from a three-game absence Sunday, so the Chargers will get a boost in their secondary despite Leonard's continued absence.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Donte Jackson
injuryReports.returnComment: Jackson missed each of the Chargers' past three games due to a hamstring injury, but he was able to log a full practice session Friday and is set to return to action versus Houston. Before getting hurt, he started in three of his four appearances to begin the season, so he'll likely return to that role Sunday, especially since fellow cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) has been ruled out.
injuryReports.injury: Jackson (hamstring) does not have a designation for Sunday's tilt against the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Brenen Thompson
injuryReports.returnComment: Thompson was not able to practice at all during the week as he continued to nurse quad and hamstring injuries, and it appears likely he'll be absent for his sixth straight game in Week 9. Unless he's able to make a surprise turnaround by Sunday, Derius Davis figures to continue to see a few extra reps at wide receiver.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: David Njoku
injuryReports.returnComment: Njoku returned to practice this week but never advanced from limited participation to full. He could have a real shot next week when the Chargers face the Ravens. In the meantime, Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will get most of the TE snaps for Los Angeles.
injuryReports.injury: Lower Leg

injuryReports.name: Kayode Awosika
injuryReports.returnComment: doubtful
injuryReports.injury: Lower Leg

injuryReports.name: Daiyan Henley
injuryReports.returnComment: Henley was dinged up in Sunday's loss to the Rams but was able to return to the contest, and it appears he'll all set for the Week 9 tilt against the Texans. Henley has posted 41 tackles (17 solo), including 0.5 sacks, two fumble recoveries, a forced fumble and one pass breakup across seven starts this season.
injuryReports.injury: Henley (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.

injuryReports.name: KeAndre Lambert-Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Lambert-Smith was expected to revert back to a minimal role on offense in Week 8 due to both Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris returning to action, and that is exactly what happened. Lambert-Smith played just two offensive snaps in the contest, and he will continue to have little to no fantasy value as long as the rest of the Chargers' primary pass catchers are healthy.
injuryReports.injury: Lambert-Smith did not garner a target during Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.

injuryReports.name: Charlie Kolar
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end's four targets tied for third on the team, as he ran 17 routes on Justin Herbert's 37 dropbacks against Los Angeles. More of a blocker than receiver, Kolar has been forced to catch more passes out of necessity at times this season. He has 10 grabs for 98 yards on 17 targets. The catches and targets are both career highs in his fifth season.
injuryReports.injury: Kolar caught one of four targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.

injuryReports.name: Tre' Harris
injuryReports.returnComment: After missing Week 6 with a hamstring injury, Harris was healthy coming out of the Week 7 bye but played pretty clearly behind both Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston against the Rams. Harris ran just 20 routes to McConkey's 34 and Johnston's 30. Harris would see a big boost if Johnston gets traded ahead of next week's deadline.
injuryReports.injury: Harris caught all three of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.

injuryReports.name: Keaton Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: Handpicked by first-year OC Mike McDaniel as a free-agent signing in the offseason, Mitchell has been a total non-factor for much of the first half of the season. With a career 5.7 yards per carry average, Mitchell is averaging just 3.7 yards per rush this season. Involved in a three-way backfield committee with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal, Mitchell is waiver-wire fodder in normal-sized 12-team fantasy leagues.
injuryReports.injury: Mitchell rushed four times for six yards and caught all three of his targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.

injuryReports.name: Cameron Dicker
injuryReports.returnComment: The Chargers offense put forth another poor effort in Week 8, with four of their 11 drives ending in punts and another three ending with turnovers. Dicker has mostly been efficient through his first seven games of the season, making 12 of his 14 field-goal attempts, but until the offense demonstrates it can consistently move the ball down the field, he'll be hard to trust as a fantasy option.
injuryReports.injury: Dicker made all three of his field-goal attempts during Sunday's 24-9 loss against the Rams. He did not kick any extra-point tries.

injuryReports.name: Kimani Vidal
injuryReports.returnComment: The Chargers continue to use a fantasy-unfriendly three-man backfield, giving all three of Vidal, Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell meaningful touches and snaps. In a broken Los Angeles offense and crowded group of RBs, Vidal has minimal fantasy appeal outside of deeper formats.
injuryReports.injury: Vidal rushed eight times for 23 yards and caught both of his targets for seven yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.

injuryReports.name: Quentin Johnston
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnston's four grabs marked a new personal single-game high through six games this season. One of the least efficient wideouts in the league, Johnston entered Sunday with just eight grabs for 165 yards on 22 targets. He hasn't been playable in fantasy football for weeks and will square off with a stingy Houston secondary in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Johnston caught all four of his targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.

injuryReports.name: Oronde Gadsden
injuryReports.returnComment: Gadsden was able to lead the team in catches while he finished with one fewer target than team leader Ladd McConkey. The tight end has now reeled in at least three passes for the second straight game and third time over the last four contests after having failed to do so in any of the team's first three regular-season games. Gadsden and the rest of the Chargers will face a tough test in Week 9 against the Texans.
injuryReports.injury: Gadsden caught all five of his targets for 52 yards during Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.

injuryReports.name: Omarion Hampton
injuryReports.returnComment: Hampton logged just one more carry than Kimani Vidal and five more than Keaton Mitchell, as the Chargers' ground game continued to resemble a committee scenario. Hampton now has 45 rushing yards or fewer in four straight games, and he's logged single-digit carries in three of those contests. The second-year back is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry behind an injury-hampered offensive line as well, leaving his outlook bleak for a Week 9 home matchup against an aggressive Texans defense next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Hampton rushed nine times for 20 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Chargers' 24-9 loss to the Rams on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Ladd McConkey
injuryReports.returnComment: McConkey finally shook off the concussion that led to his exit from a Week 6 loss to the Chiefs during Week 8 prep, and despite the fact Tre' Harris also was back from a hamstring injury, the former still led the Chargers in receiving yards and targets. The yardage tally was also a season high for McConkey, who is averaging a career-best 16.8 YPC on his 17 catches to date. Los Angeles' air attack showed some improvement Sunday following some retooling during the Week 7 bye, and McConkey figures to remain the top target on the winless Bolts in a Week 9 home matchup against the Texans next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: McConkey brought in four of six targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 24-9 loss to the Rams on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Justin Herbert
injuryReports.returnComment: The Chargers declined to move on from offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel during the Week 7 bye, and Herbert did finish with a season-high passing yardage total on a season-best 75.0 percent completion rate. However, Herbert failed to throw a touchdown pass for the second straight game while tossing multiple interceptions for the third time this season. Herbert still has just a 61.8 percent completion rate -- a career low by a fairly wide margin -- and a 5:10 TD:INT through seven games as the winless Bolts try again for their first victory in a Week 9 home matchup against the Texans next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Herbert completed 24 of 32 passes for 257 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions while rushing four times for 15 yards in the Chargers' 24-9 loss to the Rams on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that remained with the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Derwin James Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: James missed the Chargers' three games prior to the Week 7 bye due to a hamstring injury. He suffered a setback in his recovery during Week 8 prep, which will require a stint on IR for the veteran safety. James is required to be sidelined for at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29. Tony Jefferson will continue to operate in an elevated role in the secondary in James' absence.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Joe Alt
injuryReports.returnComment: Alt missed the Chargers' last two games before their bye in Week 7 because of a neck injury he suffered back in Week 4 at Seattle, but he is now on track to play Sunday against the Rams. He should start at one of the Chargers' tackle spots opposite rookie fourth-rounder Travis Burke in Week 8.
injuryReports.injury: Alt (neck) was not listed on the Chargers' official injury report Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Joe Cardona
injuryReports.returnComment: Cardona continues to struggle with an ankle injury and will now miss a second straight week. Jake McQuaide will once again operate as the Rams' long snapper in Sunday's contest.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Ty Simpson
injuryReports.returnComment: Simpson will once again be inactive behind quarterbacks Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett. The first-round rookie will only be eligible to play if both Stafford and Bennett exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Kam Curl
injuryReports.returnComment: Curl is set to suit up for Sunday's game despite missing the Rams' Wednesday and Thursday practice sessions. The strong safety will need to anchor the team's secondary due to the absence of starting cornerbacks Jaylen Watson (shoulder, IR) and Trent McDuffie (back).
injuryReports.injury: Curl (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Trent McDuffie
injuryReports.returnComment: McDuffie will miss his third game of the season due to injury. The star cornerback played 80 percent of the defensive snaps in the Rams' Week 8 win over the Chargers but picked up a back injury during the victory. With Jaylen Watson (shoulder) on IR, the Rams' starting corners against the Commanders will likely be Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Colby Parkinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Parkinson, who was inactive in Week 8, managed to log a limited practice Friday, before being listed as questionable for the contest. With Terrance Ferguson (ankle) -- who was initially slated to return to action this week -- but subsequently ruled out -- still not in the mix, the return of Parkinson -- who has caught five passes in each of the last two games he played -- is a welcome boost to a Rams TE corps that also includes Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and Max Klare.
injuryReports.injury: Parkinson (ribs) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Whittington
injuryReports.returnComment: Whittington was a limited participant throughout Week 9 prep as he dealt with a back injury. The kick returner and No. 4 wide receiver for the Rams is all set to suit up for Sunday's game as he looks to play through the issue.
injuryReports.injury: Whittington (back) is active for Sunday's game against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Keagen Trost
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Bill Murray
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Darryl Peterson III
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Desjuan Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Watson
injuryReports.returnComment: Watson exited Sunday's win over the Chargers early with a severe shoulder injury. The cornerback will undergo surgery while on IR, which will end his season. Watson ends the season with 24 tackles (14 solo) and nine passes defensed, including one interception, over seven regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Ronnie Rivers
injuryReports.returnComment: Rivers missed six games while on injured reserve with a calf injury he sustained in the Rams' Week 2 loss to the Giants. The 27-year-old has returned ahead of Sunday's game against the Commanders and has no injury designation headed into the contest. Rivers will likely be a special-teams contributor with no real role in the Rams' offense.
injuryReports.injury: The Rams activated Rivers (calf) from injured reserve Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Myles Garrett
injuryReports.returnComment: Garrett thus is in the clear for his first game action since Week 1, after which he required arthroscopic surgery on his left knee and an IR stint that sidelined him the last seven contests. Sunday's outing will mark his first working with the out-of-retirement Aaron Donald, and while Garrett may be hard-pressed to extend his streak of 10-plus sack seasons to nine the rest of the way, he should provide a boost to the Rams' fifth-ranked defense (301.1 yards per game).
injuryReports.injury: Garrett (knee) was activated from injured reserve Saturday and doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Washington.

injuryReports.name: Terrance Ferguson
injuryReports.returnComment: Ferguson made it back from his ankle injury, only to be sidelined by another concern two days before he was set for a return to game action. The Rams could use him, as they haven't found a second consistent receiving threat alongside Puka Nacua in the absence of Davante Adams (IR - hamstring). Another absence for Ferguson leaves Tyler Higbee as well as  Colby Parkinson (ribs, questionable), if available, as the Rams' tight top ends, with Davis Allen and Max Klare providing extra bodies for multi-TE sets.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Quentin Lake
injuryReports.returnComment: Lake was able to secure exactly seven takedowns for the third straight week, as he has now registered six or more tackles in every game this season. The 27-year-old's biggest moment of the contest came in the first quarter, when he jumped in front of a short pass from Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert for his third interception of the year. Lake has now compiled 56 total tackles (34 solo), a forced fumble, and 11 passes defensed, three of which are interceptions, over eight games so far in the regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Lake recorded seven total tackles (two solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 24-9 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Joshua Karty
injuryReports.returnComment: Karty was elevated from the practice squad for each of the Rams' previous two games and handled kickoff duties while Brandon McManus kicked field goals and extra points. That arrangement isn't expected to change moving forward, per Nate Adkins of The Athletic, so it would likely take a McManus slump or injury for Karty to get a shot at the fantasy-relevant aspects of the kicker position.
injuryReports.injury: The Rams signed Karty to their active roster Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Matthew Stafford
injuryReports.returnComment: Stafford was seen leaving the locker room with his upper right arm wrapped in ice after this past Sunday's win against the Chargers. Head coach Sean McVay told Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register on Monday that Stafford has been tending to arm soreness, but the quarterback clarified the situation with Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times on Wednesday, stating that he's had his right arm wrapped in ice regularly this season. An uncapped session to begin Week 9 prep puts Stafford in the clear to continue to lead the Ram's offense Sunday in Washington.
injuryReports.injury: Stafford (right elbow) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Higbee
injuryReports.returnComment: Higbee logged a hearty 83 percent offensive snap share, most among Rams tight ends. However, he got little attention from quarterback Matthew Stafford, recording just two targets. Higbee had a nice run in Weeks 3-5, when he logged 18 catches for 212 yards across the three-game span. However, since then he's posted just seven receptions for 50 yards across his subsequent three contests. As such, it's hard to trust Higbee on a week-to-week basis right now even with the Rams down multiple pass catchers in Davante Adams (hamstring - IR), Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) and Colby Parkinson (ribs).
injuryReports.injury: Higbee caught one of two targets for 14 yards against the Chargers in Sunday's 24-9 victory.

injuryReports.name: Dean Connors
injuryReports.returnComment: Connors broke his hand in Sunday's win over the Chargers and is slated for surgery. He's worked as a core special-teamer this season but hasn't logged a snap on offense. As such, Connors' IR stint -- which will last at least four games -- isn't likely to cause any waves in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Hand

injuryReports.name: Brandon McManus
injuryReports.returnComment: While Joshua Karty handled kickoffs for the Rams, McManus was entrusted with field goals and extra-point tries. The kicker's first field-goal attempt with his new team was a 30-yarder, so the veteran player has not yet been challenged as a Ram.
injuryReports.injury: McManus converted his sole field-goal attempt and all three PATs in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Blake Corum
injuryReports.returnComment: Corum led the Rams in rushing yards despite logging five fewer carries than Kyren Williams, and, like the latter, Corum was able to get into the end zone. Corum's score came early in the third quarter on a winding 23-yard run, his second in as many games. The third-year back now has double-digit carries in consecutive games for the second time this season, and he's averaging a career-best 5.2 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Corum rushed 11 times for 73 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Kyren Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams had a difficult time finding running room against a game Chargers defense, but he salvaged his fantasy day with a one-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter. Williams has five of his six rushing scores on the season in the last four games, and he's still averaging a robust 4.9 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Williams rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a touchdown and brought in his sole target for three yards in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Puka Nacua
injuryReports.returnComment: Nacua unsurprisingly led the Rams across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets and did so by a wide margin. With Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) unavailable for the last two games, Nacua has drawn 22 total targets and scored twice, with Sunday's touchdown coming on an 18-yard catch-and-run in the latter portion of the third quarter. Nacua is being used in a shorter-area role than past seasons -- he's averaging a career-low 10.1 yards per catch -- but he'll remain an elite fantasy option in a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Nacua secured 11 of 12 targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Kaytron Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen is officially active for Sunday's matchup against the Lions after finishing the week with full participation in practice Friday. The 23-year-old plays a majority of his snaps on special teams and will likely have the same role in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Allen is listed as active for Sunday's matchup against the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Wright
injuryReports.returnComment: After sitting out Wednesday's practice due to a quadriceps injury, Wright was able to get back to limited Thursday and maintain that activity level Friday, at which point he was tagged as questionable in advance of the weekend. On Sunday morning, however, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Wright isn't expected to suit up, and that's now locked in. With Wright out of the lineup, Kaytron Allen (quad) and Carlos Washington will serve as the reserve RB options behind Ollie Gordon.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Reese Taylor
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Jalen Tolbert
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Chukwuebuka Godrick
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Christian Haynes
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Justin Joly
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Marcellas Dial Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Carlos Washington Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Washington's elevation is his second of the campaign. He was active for Week 5 and logged nine offensive snaps, along with three special-teams snaps, against Cincinnati, but he finished without any touches or targets. His workload against the Lions will likely depend on whether Jaylen Wright and Kaytron Allen, both of whom are questionable due to quad injuries, are able to suit up.
injuryReports.injury: Miami elevated Washington from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's tilt against Detroit.

injuryReports.name: Zane Gonzalez
injuryReports.returnComment: Gonzalez has worked as Miami's gameday kicker each of the past two weeks and will do so again versus Detroit on Sunday. He's performed adequately so far, going 2-for-3 on field-goal tries and 5-for-5 on extra-point attempts. This is Gonzalez's third and final elevation, so the Dolphins would need to sign him to the active roster to continue having him kick in games beyond this weekend.
injuryReports.injury: The Dolphins elevated Gonzalez from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Kadyn Proctor
injuryReports.returnComment: Proctor suffered a concussion in Week 7 against the Jets and didn't play this past Sunday versus New England. However, he was a full participant in all three of Miami's practices this week and has cleared concussion protocol. Proctor is therefore set to reclaim his starting role at left guard.
injuryReports.injury: Proctor (concussion) does not have a designation for Sunday's Week 9 matchup versus Detroit, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.

injuryReports.name: Will Kacmarek
injuryReports.returnComment: Kacmarek played through his lingering hamstring issue in Week 8 versus the Patriots, and after practicing in full Friday, it looks like he's good to go for Week 9 as well. He should continue to operate as the Dolphins' second option at tight end behind starter Greg Dulcich.
injuryReports.injury: Kacmarek (hamstring) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Lions, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.

injuryReports.name: Jacob Rodriguez
injuryReports.returnComment: Rodriguez fell three tackles shy of Jordyn Brooks' team-leading total as the Dolphins dropped to 1-6. The rookie second-round pick's 12 tackles over the past two games mark the most fallow two-game stretch of Rodriguez's young career in that category. He'll try to pick up the pace in Week 9 against the Lions.
injuryReports.injury: Rodriguez notched eight tackles (two solo) and forced a fumble in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.

injuryReports.name: Jordyn Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: Brooks led the Dolphins in tackles during the loss, which dropped Miami's record to 1-6. The 29-year-old linebacker has slowed down a bit after leading the NFL with 183 tackles (99 solo) during the 2025 regular season, though he's still averaging a respectable nine tackles per game in 2026. He could draw interest on the trade market from contending teams in search of help at linebacker.
injuryReports.injury: Brooks recorded 11 tackles (six solo) in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.

injuryReports.name: Darrell Baker Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Baker has been on the reserve/PUP list since Aug. 31 after suffering an undisclosed injury in July. The cornerback is eligible to have his 21-day practice window opened and begin practicing at any point, but he doesn't appear to be healthy enough to do so yet.
injuryReports.injury: Undisclosed

injuryReports.name: Malik Washington
injuryReports.returnComment: The five grabs led the team on the afternoon, and Washington capped his performance with a one-yard TD from Malik Willis just before halftime. It was Washington's first score of the season in seven games, and he'll take a 31-329-1 line on 45 targets into a Week 9 meeting with the Lions.
injuryReports.injury: Washington caught five of six targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-19 loss to New England.

injuryReports.name: Kevin Coleman Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Coleman led the team in receiving yards while reeling in multiple passes for the second time this season. The wide receiver's biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he connected with quarterback Malik Willis for a 35-yard score with 2:04 remaining in regulation. Coleman hasn't been a consistent part of the team's offensive approach this season, catching eight of 21 targets for 82 yards and two scores over seven contests so far.
injuryReports.injury: Coleman caught all three of his targets for 46 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.

injuryReports.name: Odell Beckham Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Beckham kicked off the season with the Giants but was targeted just one time through the first three contests before the team released him Sept. 29. He then joined the Vikings on the practice squad and was elevated for Week 5 but eventually was inactive. Thus, if Beckham is able to avoid such a listing Monday against the Bills, it'll mark the sixth different organization in which he's suited up in his career.
injuryReports.injury: The Vikings are signing Beckham from the practice squad to the active roster, Tom Pelissero of NFL Network reports.

injuryReports.name: Andrew Van Ginkel
injuryReports.returnComment: Van Ginkel was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday but was able to upgrade to full participation Saturday. He's thus clear to suit up on Monday Night Football against the Bills. That's a big deal for the Vikings in their quest to slow down Josh Allen, as Van Ginkel leads the team with 6.5 sacks through seven games.
injuryReports.injury: Van Ginkel (chest) doesn't have a designation for Monday's matchup against the Bills, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Demond Claiborne
injuryReports.returnComment: Claiborne didn't practice Friday or Saturday after suffering a knee injury in practice Wednesday. Head coach Kevin O'Connell said he doesn't think Claiborne will need surgery but added that the team is still evaluating the injury. The running back has played sparingly this season, logging 18 offensive snaps through four games and tallying 13 yards on six carries along with eight yards on two receptions.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jauan Jennings
injuryReports.returnComment: Per head coach Kevin O'Connell, Jennings suffered a calf injury at Thursday's practice that is serious enough to sideline him for at least one game. Jennings' next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 15 in Green Bay, while Tai Felton and Myles Price are in for some offensive snaps this week behind the top WR duo of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Kyler Murray
injuryReports.returnComment: Murray emerged from last Sunday's loss to the Lions with a sore hamstring, and O'Connell told Alec Lewis of The Athletic on Thursday that the quarterback was unlikely to play in Week 9 but also wasn't an IR consideration. Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported Saturday morning that Murray is in recovery mode from a Grade 2 hamstring strain that will sideline him Monday and potentially beyond that point. Now that Murray officially is out for his second contest of the campaign, Carson Wentz is set to see his first game action since Week 2.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Christian Darrisaw
injuryReports.returnComment: Darrisaw began Week 9 prep with a limited session Thursday, but he was able to log a full session Friday. As such, he should be good to go for Monday's matchup against Buffalo.
injuryReports.injury: Darrisaw (shoulder) was a full practice participant Friday.

injuryReports.name: Jay Ward
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Max Brosmer
injuryReports.returnComment: It would likely take an injury to Wentz for Brosmer to get into the game, but the latter moves one step closer to getting on the field for the first time in 2026. Brosmer didn't look like an NFL-caliber QB as a rookie in 2025, posting a 0:4 TD:INT across seven appearances, including two starts.
injuryReports.injury: Brosmer is set to back up Carson Wentz against the Bills on Monday, as Kyler Murray (hamstring) won't play, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Carson Wentz
injuryReports.returnComment: Wentz will get the Week 9 assignment at QB for the Vikings, with Kyler Murray viewed as week-to-week with a hamstring strain, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Max Brosmer will be the team's backup versus Buffalo, and perhaps longer than that should Murray's injury linger. Wentz thus represents an option for those in Superflex formats or otherwise are in need of signal-caller help due to injury or bye week issues.
injuryReports.injury: Wentz is stated to start Monday night's game against the Bills, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

injuryReports.name: DeeJay Dallas
injuryReports.returnComment: Dallas will return to the active roster after playing in the first five contests of the year with the Vikings before being released and ultimately returning to the team as a member of the practice squad in late October. The running back has rushed four times for 14 yards and caught all four of his targets for 34 yards over seven contests with Minnesota this year, and he figures to operate in an extreme depth role behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason on Monday night versus Buffalo.
injuryReports.injury: Dallas was signed to the Vikings' active roster Wednesday, Craig Peters of the team's official website reports.

injuryReports.name: Eric Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson finished second on the Vikings in stops, behind only Josh Metellus (13). One of his tackles was a sack of Jared Goff for a 10-yard loss on Detroit's first drive of the game, resulting in a Detroit punt. Wilson has 3.0 sacks through seven games, so he could surpass the career-best mark of 6.5 sacks he recorded over 17 regular-season games last year.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson registered 11 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, in Sunday's loss to Detroit.

injuryReports.name: Joshua Metellus
injuryReports.returnComment: Metellus led Minnesota in tackles and recorded a season-high mark in the process. He's been a consistent presence for the Vikings' tough defense this season, playing every defensive snap in six of the team's seven contests so far. Metellus is up to 50 stops through seven games, putting him on pace for the third triple-digit tackle campaign of his career.
injuryReports.injury: Metellus recorded 13 tackles (six solo) and a defensed pass in a Week 8 defeat against Detroit.

injuryReports.name: Byron Murphy Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Murphy tied for third on Minnesota in tackles on a day when four Vikings finished with double-digit stops. The tackle tally was Murphy's highest of the season and snapped a four-game stretch of posting three stops or fewer. The veteran cornerback is enjoying a nice campaign overall, as he's tallied three interceptions so far, tying for second in the NFL in that category.
injuryReports.injury: Murphy registered 10 tackles (eight solo) in a loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Blake Cashman
injuryReports.returnComment: Cashman was one of four Vikings to notch double-digit stops in the team's first loss of the season. The veteran linebacker has recorded at least seven stops in each of his seven games this season and has registered double-digit tackles three times. He's well beyond pace for a fourth consecutive season of triple-digit tackles, as he already has 64 stops (including 4.5 sacks) through seven contests.
injuryReports.injury: Cashman finished Sunday's loss to Detroit with 10 tackles (five solo).

injuryReports.name: Will Reichard
injuryReports.returnComment: Reichard missed a 57-yard field goal on the first drive of the game. The kicker's miss proved costly as the Vikings lost a four-point game that went down to the wire. Reichard is now 18-for-20 on field-goal attempts and 10-for-10 on PATs through seven regular-season games in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Reichard missed his sole field-goal attempt and made his sole PAT in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: T.J. Hockenson
injuryReports.returnComment: Hockenson secured an eight-yard touchdown midway through the fourth quarter to give the Vikings a 15-12 lead, and he's now up to 31 grabs for 295 yards and three touchdowns on 37 targets through seven games this season. Hockenson, though, missed all but two offensive snaps in the Week 5 win over the Saints after suffering a concussion. A favorite target for Kyler Murray in the middle and short areas of the field, Hockenson has settled in as a lower-end TE1 in fantasy. He gets a plus matchup with the Bills next Monday night in another spot the Minnesota offense may be forced to push the gas pedal.
injuryReports.injury: Hockenson caught four of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Addison
injuryReports.returnComment: Addison's big play was a 51-yard catch over the top of the defense in the fourth quarter to set the offense up at the 10-yard line. T.J. Hockenson scored a go-ahead touchdown two plays later. Addison's eight targets on the day were one fewer than Justin Jefferson, but it was the former who paced the team in receiving yards. Playing in a Minnesota offense that doesn't push the ball down the field much or focus on its outside receivers, Addison has just 16 catches for 249 yards and one touchdown on 33 targets through six games this season. He'll be a fantasy WR4 with upside next Monday night against a leaky Bills secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Addison caught three of eight targets for 66 yards in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones shook off the knee injury that had knocked him out of a Week 7 win over the Colts to head into Sunday without a designation. However, the veteran finished with a season low in carries and rushing yards. Jones has just 13 combined rush attempts -- a number partly influenced by the aforementioned early exit against Indianapolis -- in the two games since Jordan Mason returned from injured reserve, and it remains to be seen if the modest role will persist in a Week 9 home matchup against the Bills on Monday night, Nov. 9.
injuryReports.injury: Jones rushed five times for 22 yards and brought in both targets for 18 yards in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Mason
injuryReports.returnComment: Playing in his second game since returning from an IR stint due to a thumb injury, Mason paced the Vikings' ground attack in carries but finished two yards behind Aaron Jones, who logged five totes. Mason also wasn't targeted for the second time in three games, and Minnesota's running game figures to continue in a fantasy-averse timeshare between the two. Mason will look to make inroads against what has been an improved Bills run defense in a Week 9 home showdown on Monday night, Nov. 9.
injuryReports.injury: Mason rushed eight times for 20 yards in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Hunter Henry
injuryReports.returnComment: Henry practiced only once all week and it was a limited appearance Friday, but there is reason to believe he will be available Sunday. His status for Week 9 will officially be revealed when the Patriots release their inactives 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Greg Van Roten
injuryReports.returnComment: Van Roten was placed on IR due to a hamstring issue in late September before being designated to return Wednesday. He was limited in all three practices this week, and New England has elected to hold him out of gameday action for at least another week. Van Roten's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Detroit.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Mack Hollins
injuryReports.returnComment: Hollins exited a Week 4 win at Buffalo in the third quarter due to a calf injury and eventually landed on IR prior to Week 5 action. He thus has missed the requisite four games while on the list, but his status now bears watching ahead of Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. With fellow WR A.J. Brown (knee) sidelined, an active Hollins could step into a prominent role in the Patriots passing game alongside position mate DeMario Douglas.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Gabe Jacas
injuryReports.returnComment: Jacas made an early exit last Sunday versus Miami due to a knee issue. He was limited in the first two Patriots practices this week but was able to upgrade to full participation Friday, clearing the way for him to suit up in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Jacas (knee) does not have a designation for Sunday's contest versus Green Bay.

injuryReports.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
injuryReports.returnComment: Henderson will miss a second straight game tending to medical issue. With the second-year running back out last week against Miami, Stevenson logged 76.7 percent of the offensive snaps and handled a season-high 19 carries, turning them into 82 scoreless yards. He also caught three passes on three targets. Stevenson will be a volume-driven, home-favorite RB1/2 for fantasy against Green Bay, while Corey Kiner will step into the RB2 role again.
injuryReports.injury: With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) ruled out for Week 9, Stevenson is set to handle an expanded workload Sunday against the Packers, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.

injuryReports.name: TreVeyon Henderson
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Mark Daniels of MassLive.com, Mike Vrabel said that the Patriots won't put a timeline on Henderson's return, while adding, per Lazar, that the team is "just trying to make sure that TreVeyon is cared for and his recovery plan is intact and he's comfortable with it." In the absence of Henderson -- who recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms" -- Rhamondre Stevenson will pace New England's backfield, with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison also mixing in.
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: A.J. Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: With three consecutive DNPs looming, Brown doesn't seem likely to be available Sunday against the Packers. If Brown is ruled out later Friday, the stage would be set for DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, Kyle Williams and potentially Mack Hollins (calf) -- who has been designated to return from IR -- to handle New England's Week 9 WR duties.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Brenden Schooler
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Morgan Moses
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Efton Chism III
injuryReports.returnComment: Chism led the team in targets and receptions, with A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) unavailable. The wide receiver played a season-high 88 percent of the team's offensive snaps, and he has now reeled in 15 of 20 targets for 151 yards and a touchdown over seven regular-season contests with New England so far this year.
injuryReports.injury: Chism caught all five of his targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Corey Kiner
injuryReports.returnComment: Kiner operated as the top reserve option behind starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson in Week 8, with TreVeyon Henderson (illness) sidelined. Kiner has compiled 160 rushing yards on 28 carries while reeling in his only target for seven yards over the team's last four contests, and he could earn more opportunities moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: Kiner rushed seven times for 38 yards during Sunday's 24-19 win over Miami.

injuryReports.name: Marcus Bryant
injuryReports.returnComment: Bryant will return to action in Week 9 after spending the entirety of the regular season to this point on IR after suffering an ankle injury during the preseason. The 24-year-old will operate as a top reserve option behind Will Campbell and Morgan Moses at offensive tackle moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: Bryant (ankle) was activated from injured reserve by the Patriots on Tuesday.

injuryReports.name: Andy Borregales
injuryReports.returnComment: Borregales missed a 40-yard field goal during the Patriots' last drive of the first half. The kicker continues to struggle in the intermediate range, now sitting at 7-for-10 on field-goal attempts from 30-49 yards during the 2026 regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Borregales made one of his two field goals and all three PATs in the Patriots' 24-19 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Eli Raridon
injuryReports.returnComment: Raridon's lone reception went for five yards early in the first quarter. He didn't record another catch for the remainder of the contest despite logging a hefty 93 percent offensive snap share, largely due to No .1 tight end Hunter Henry departing in the first half due to a foot injury. Should Henry remain sidelined in Week 9, Raridon will have another big opportunity to produce in a home tilt against Green Bay.
injuryReports.injury: Raridon had one reception for five yards on four targets in New England's 24-19 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams made the most of his only touch in Week 8, scoring on a 43-yard deep ball from Drake Maye in the third quarter. The wide receiver had an opportunity to be more involved with A.J. Brown (knee) sidelined Sunday, but Williams saw just one target for the third game in a row. On the year, the wide receiver has now caught seven of 13 targets for 190 yards and two touchdowns over eight regular-season contests.
injuryReports.injury: Williams caught his lone target for a 43-yard touchdown during Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: DeMario Douglas
injuryReports.returnComment: Most of his production came on a nifty 48-yard catch-and-run in the fourth quarter, as Douglas took a strike from Drake Maye along the sideline but then curled back toward the middle of the field and dashed the remaining 30 yards to the end zone while out-racing four Miami defenders. It was the fourth touchdown of the season for the fourth-year wideout, a new career high, and Douglas will take a 26-332-4 line on 37 targets through eight games into a Week 9 tilt against the Packers.
injuryReports.injury: Douglas caught all three of his targets for 76 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Drake Maye
injuryReports.returnComment: While he failed to reach 200 passing yards for the third time in eight games this season, Maye put together a very efficient performance as he produced multiple TDs for a fifth straight game. All three scores came in the second half as the QB rallied the Patriots from a 13-3 deficit, hitting Kyle Williams for a 43-yard score in the third quarter and DeMario Douglas for a 48-yard strike in the fourth, while running for a two-yard TD in between. Maye appears to have gotten his recklessness under control, committing just one turnover in the last four contests, and he'll take a 15:8 TD:INT on the season into a Week 9 clash with the Packers.
injuryReports.injury: Maye completed 16 of 20 passes for 199 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins. He added five rushing yards and a TD on eight carries.

injuryReports.name: Zach Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: The former Jet remains the odd-quarterback out for the Saints. Wilson will not be allowed to play in Sunday's contest unless both Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Tyler Shough
injuryReports.returnComment: As Johnson notes, Shough wasn't listed on the Saints' Week 9 injury report, as he was (as a full participant) in Week 7, prior to the team's bye. With no reported reported setbacks, Shough -- who sustained two broken bones in his left (on-throwing) hand Oct. 5 -- is presumably simply protecting his hand until it's 100 percent healed. On the plus side from the QB's perspective as he continues to play through the issue, is that highly-touted rookie WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) -- the eighth overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft -- is making his much-awaited regular-season debut for New Orleans.
injuryReports.injury: Shough was still wearing a glove on his left hand during pregame warmups ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns, according to Luke Johnson of The New Orleans Times-Picayune.

injuryReports.name: Martin Emerson Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Emerson didn't participate in Friday's practice after kicking off the week limited Wednesday and Thursday. He appears to be ready to go, as he's not on the Saints' list of inactive players. The 26-year-old has 18 total tackles (16 solo), four pass deflections and two interceptions in six games.
injuryReports.injury: Emerson is listed as active for Sunday's matchup against the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Jordyn Tyson
injuryReports.returnComment: Tyson, the eighth overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, injured his hamstring in August, but now those who held onto to the highly-touted rookie during his absence a" or recently added him to their roster a" will going forward have a player with a high ceiling to consider for fantasy lineups. Given the long layoff, the Saints could choose to proceed deliberately with Tyson in his NFL regular-season debut, but as the season rolls along, the Arizona State product should yield dividends working alongside top pass-catcher Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele, who had been working as the team's WR2 in Tyson's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Tyson (hamstring) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Browns, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.

injuryReports.name: Mason Murphy
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Mike Reid
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: John Ridgeway III
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Jaylan Ford
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Christen Miller
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: CJ Donaldson
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Kelvin Banks Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Banks landed on IR in late September and was initially expected to be sidelined at least 10 weeks. He could beat that timeline by a considerable margin if he suits up Sunday, though his status may not ultimately be known until about 90 minutes prior to tipoff. If he does play, Banks will likely slide back into the starting left tackle role ahead of Asim Richards (ankle), who is also questionable.
injuryReports.injury: The Saints activated Banks (ankle) from injured reserve Saturday, and he remains questionable to play Sunday versus Cleveland.

injuryReports.name: Zamir White
injuryReports.returnComment: White has been on New Orleans' practice squad all season, waiting for a gameday opportunity. He'll get that chance Sunday after Kendre Miller was waived Saturday and CJ Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) was ruled out from facing the Browns. With that said, White may not get an extensive look, as Alvin Kamara and possibly Audric Estime are ahead of him on the RB depth chart.
injuryReports.injury: The Saints elevated White from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's matchup against Cleveland.

injuryReports.name: Charlie Smyth
injuryReports.returnComment: Smyth is set to take over as New Orleans' kicker beginning with Sunday's matchup against Cleveland, so the elevation was a necessary move. He'll be replacing Daniel Carlson, who was released Tuesday. The Browns have had 19 field-goal tries against them this season, tied for eighth-most in the NFL, so Smyth could be busy in his 2026 debut.
injuryReports.injury: The Saints elevated Smyth from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Justin Reid
injuryReports.returnComment: Reid was a full participant in all three Week 9 practice sessions. The Saints' starting strong safety has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the Browns.
injuryReports.injury: Reid (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Alvin Kamara
injuryReports.returnComment: Kamara went from DNP due to rest/back Wednesday to limited Thursday and finally full Friday, paving the way for him to be available to the Saints backfield. With fellow RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) sidelined this weekend, it'll be Kamara and Kendre Miller to handle the load Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Kamara (rest/back) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Cesar Ruiz
injuryReports.returnComment: Ruiz missed the Saints' pre-bye game against the Steelers in Paris, but the two weeks off were apparently enough to get him ready for Week 9 against Cleveland.
injuryReports.injury: Ruiz (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Nathan Shepherd
injuryReports.returnComment: Shepherd hasn't played since Week 4 but appears ready to return for Sunday's game against the Browns. He has 12 tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, across 175 defensive snaps this season.
injuryReports.injury: Shepherd (illness) practiced in full Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Travis Etienne Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Etienne has missed the required four games on IR due to a strained left hamstring, but even with the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he hasn't gained clearance to mix into drills. Moore told Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana on Monday that Etienne has a chance to return to practice this week, but with no on-field work to begin Week 9 prep, he seems to be on the outside looking in to have enough time to be activated for Sunday's contest against the Browns.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Audric Estime
injuryReports.returnComment: New Orleans released kicker Daniel Carlson to clear room on the 53-man roster for Estime, who began the season with the Saints before being cut on an injury settlement Sept. 22. After moving past a thigh injury, Estime caught on with the Browns and made his lone appearance for the team back in Week 6, when he carried nine times for 19 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Ravens. Upon rejoining the Saints, Estime will provide depth to a backfield that also includes Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson (shoulder).
injuryReports.injury: The Saints claimed Estime off waivers from the Browns on Tuesday.

injuryReports.name: Carl Granderson
injuryReports.returnComment: Granderson helped keep the game close with a pair of key sacks. He brought down Aaron Rodgers near the end of the second quarter to help hold the Steelers to a field goal, then split a sack in the red zone at the end of the third period to again limit Pittsburgh to three points. Granderson is up to 5.5 sacks through six games on the campaign, giving him an excellent chance of surpassing the career-high mark of 8.5 sacks he established over 17 contests in 2023.
injuryReports.injury: Granderson totaled four tackles, including 1.5 sacks, in Sunday's Week 7 loss to Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Pete Werner
injuryReports.returnComment: Werner had a two-game streak of double-digit stops snapped, but he was still plenty productive. The veteran linebacker dealt with a neck injury in early October but appears past that issue, as he's played every Saints defensive snap in three straight contests. Werner leads New Orleans with 54 tackles (including 2.0 sacks) through seven games.
injuryReports.injury: Werner finished Sunday's loss to the Steelers with eight tackles (three solo).

injuryReports.name: Jonas Sanker
injuryReports.returnComment: Sanker recorded his second-highest tackle tally of the campaign to lead New Orleans in that category. The second-year defender has now tallied six or more stops in five of his seven games this season. With 44 tackles through seven contests, Sanker is easily on pace to surpass the 80 stops he notched in 17 games as a rookie.
injuryReports.injury: Sanker posted nine tackles (seven solo) in Sunday's Week 7 loss to Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Noah Fant
injuryReports.returnComment: After finding the end zone twice in the loss to the Raiders in Week 3, Fant has combined for just three catches in his previous three appearances. While his two receptions Sunday were a small step in the right direction, he is expected to continue to play second fiddle to Juwan Johnson moving forward. It may also be a matter of time before rookie Oscar Delp logs more snaps from week to week.
injuryReports.injury: Fant gathered in all two targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 16-10 defeat against Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Bryce Lance
injuryReports.returnComment: Lance had two catches for the second consecutive game, though unlike the Week 6 win over the Giants, he didn't find the end zone. The 24-year-old has logged 332 offensive snaps this season, third in the receiving corps behind Chris Olave (387) and Devaughn Vele (438). However, despite being on the field more often than most of the other wideouts on the roster, Lance hasn't been productive thus far in his rookie campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Lance reeled in all two targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Charlie Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones was limited throughout Week 9 prep with a thumb injury. The wide receiver is not only active but was not wearing a cast or brace over the injured appendage as he fielded punts in pregame warmups.
injuryReports.injury: Jones (hand) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Thomas Fidone II
injuryReports.returnComment: Fidone suited up for each of New York's previous three games before a Week 8 bye, but he's a healthy scratch against the Eagles. The second-year tight end has worked mostly on special teams this season and has one catch for 29 yards on one target over three contests. Fidone figures to be at risk for inactive status when the three tight ends ahead of him in the pecking order -- Isaiah Likely, Theo Johnson and Chris Manhertz -- are healthy.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Cam Skattebo
injuryReports.returnComment: Skattebo reportedly pushed to play Sunday, but Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reported shortly before inactives were released that Skattebo would not suit up Sunday, and he was indeed ruled out for Week 9. With fellow running back Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) already sidelined, Devin Singletary will be the top option in the Giants' backfield, Phil Mafah -- also per Raanan -- will "likely be the next man up" and Greg Desrosiers will also be available as needed.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: CJ Okoye
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive

injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
