injuryReports.name: Marcus Mbow
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Phil Mafah
injuryReports.returnComment: Mafah joined New York's practice squad in mid-September, and he'll get his first chance with the club's gameday roster Sunday versus the Eagles. The Clemson product played in one game as a rookie with Dallas last season, garnering 18 yards and a touchdown on five carries along with two catches for 11 yards on two targets in Week 18. Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is doubtful to suit up Sunday, so Mafah could work in tandem with Greg Desrosiers behind Devin Singletary.
injuryReports.injury: The Giants elevated Mafah from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jalin Hyatt
injuryReports.returnComment: Hyatt was a regular part of the wideout corps with New York during his first two NFL seasons, but his role was reduced dramatically last year, and he's spent most of 2026 on the team's practice squad. He saw his first regular-season action as a practice-squad elevation in Week 7 versus Houston and played 10 total snaps (four on offense and six on special teams) without otherwise getting into the box score. Hyatt doesn't figure to see much work on offense Sunday against Philadelphia, though he could receive a slight bump if Charlie Jones (who is questionable due to a hand injury) can't suit up.
injuryReports.injury: The Giants signed Hyatt from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Andrew Thomas
injuryReports.returnComment: A lingering groin issue held Thomas to limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, but he was able to log a full session Friday to avoid a designation heading into the weekend. The star left tackle will therefore continue to anchor the offensive line for the first place Giants.
injuryReports.injury: Thomas (groin) does not have a designation for Sunday's matchup in Philadelphia.

injuryReports.name: Malik Nabers
injuryReports.returnComment: Nabers was held out of drills Thursday due to a knee injury, but his return to all activity one day later lines up with head coach John Harbaugh's assessment of the situation Friday, when he told Matt Citak of the Giants' official site that the wide receiver "practiced fully" and is "full go" for Week 9. As a result, Nabers will look to build upon the massive 36-509-2 line on 51 targets that he's accrued over the last four contests.
injuryReports.injury: Nabers (knee) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Philadelphia.

injuryReports.name: Devin Singletary
injuryReports.returnComment: Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) is on injured reserve and required to miss at least the next four games, and Najee Harris was recently released, so it'll be Singletary's job Sunday. Practice-squad types Greg Desrosiers and Phil Mafah are in tow as the backups but both have little-to-no experience carrying the ball in the NFL. Volume alone will put Singletary in the fantasy RB2 mix.
injuryReports.injury: With Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doubtful to play Week 9, Singletary is expected to operate as the Giants' lead back Sunday against the Eagles, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Greg Desrosiers Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Desrosiers is listed as running back No. 3 on the Giants' depth chart and could be in line to back up Devin Singletary on Sunday if Cam Skattebo can't play after being listed as questionable with a hamstring injury. Desrosiers has yet to play in a regular-season game this season. In three preseason games, he rushed 23 times for 166 yards and a touchdown.
injuryReports.injury: Desrosiers could serve as a backup for the Giants on Sunday, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Abdul Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter was absent Wednesday, but his return to the practice field puts the edge rusher on track for Sunday's game against the Eagles. Carter has started all seven games this season, recording 18 tackles (six solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a forced fumble on 88 percent of the defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Carter (illness) returned to practice Thursday, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Greg Newsome II
injuryReports.returnComment: Newsome is healthy again after missing the Week 7 win over the Texans due to a concussion. The 26-year-old signed a three-year extension with the team Tuesday and will resume his role as one of its starting cornerbacks during Sunday's matchup against the Eagles.
injuryReports.injury: Newsome (concussion) wasn't listed on the Giants' injury report Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Jevon Holland
injuryReports.returnComment: Holland was forced to miss the team's overtime win against the Texans in Week 7 while recovering from a concussion, but he now appears to have cleared concussion protocol. The 26-year-old will be back in his starting role in New York's secondary versus Philadelphia on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Holland (concussion) was not listed on the Giants' injury report Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Theo Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson appears to be back to full health after missing the team's last two contests while nursing a neck injury. The 25-year-old will be back in his No. 2 role at tight end behind starter Isaiah Likely against the Eagles on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson (neck) was a full participant at the Giants' practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Arvell Reese
injuryReports.returnComment: Reese continues to produce nice tackle numbers, as he's recorded seven or more stops in five of his seven games this season. The rookie out of Ohio State didn't notch a sack in his first four contests, but he's starting to pick up the pace with 1.5 sacks across his past three games. Reese has logged 100 percent of New York's defensive snaps in all but one of his appearances so far.
injuryReports.injury: Reese posted seven tackles (five solo), including 0.5 sacks, in Sunday's 27-21 overtime victory against the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Micah McFadden
injuryReports.returnComment: Among McFadden's 10 stops were two tackles for loss. The veteran linebacker had logged only three defensive snaps while serving primarily on special teams before Sunday, but he stepped into a starting role and played every one of the Giants' defensive snaps against Houston. It appears McFadden is going to be the replacement for inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, who landed on IR due to a chest injury last week.
injuryReports.injury: McFadden notched 10 tackles (all solo) in Sunday's 27-21 overtime win against the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Tyrone Tracy Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Just as general manager Joe Schoen indicated would be the case earlier in the day, Tracy was deactivated after straining his hamstring during Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans. He'll be out for at least the next four games, making the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers his earliest possible return date. While Tracy is sidelined, Devin Singletary is expected to operate as the top complement to Cam Skattebo (hamstring), who thrived while moving back into a lead role out of the backfield in the Week 7 victory.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Darnell Mooney
injuryReports.returnComment: Mooney has now been held to one or no catches in three of the past four games, and he has yet to exceed two receptions in a contest this season. The wide receiver will continue to be an unattractive fantasy option when the Giants return to action Week 9 against the Eagles.
injuryReports.injury: Mooney caught one of three targets for four yards and rushed once for three yards during Sunday's 27-21 overtime win against the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Tim Patrick
injuryReports.returnComment: Garrett Wilson is sitting out due to a concussion, but Patrick still won't suit up for Sunday's contest. The 32-year-old has been a healthy scratch the past two weeks after catching three passes for 41 yards in the previous three games.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.returnComment: inactive

injuryReports.name: Kohl Levao
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: VJ Payne
injuryReports.returnComment: Payne has been on IR all season but was designated to return Wednesday. Despite being a full participant in practice all week, he isn't quite ready for game action. Payne's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Buffalo.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Nahshon Wright
injuryReports.returnComment: Wright is dealing with a back issue that held him out of practice Friday. The issue is problematic enough to keep the veteran cornerback from suiting up Sunday. Wright's absence shouldn't have a big impact on New York's defensive rotations, as he hasn't yet logged a defensive snap through three contests this year.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Joseph Ossai
injuryReports.returnComment: Ossai managed a trio of limited practices this week and was initially deemed questionable to suit up Sunday. However, he's not yet ready to play and is going to miss his fourth straight game. Ossai's next chance to return to action is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Buffalo.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Braelon Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen averaged 18.6 carries for 100.8 yards and 0.4 TDs over the past four games, adding 2.6 catches for 14.0 yards on 3.4 targets while playing at least 78 percent of snaps each week. He won't get that kind of workload with Hall back in the lineup, but it is possible that this turns into a hot-hand situation where Allen still has a chance to take the majority of carries if he outplays his backfield mate. Both Glenn and Hall said earlier this week that Hall is still viewed as the starter.
injuryReports.injury: Jets coach Aaron Glenn declined to elaborate on the distribution of carries between Allen and Breece Hall, who will return from a five-game absence for Sunday's matchup with Kansas City, ESPN's Rich Cimini reports.

injuryReports.name: Adonai Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: Mitchell is coming off the best performance of his career -- a 7-141-1 receiving line on 26 routes (nine targets) in last week's 38-33 loss to Las Vegas. Cooper also ran 26 routes but finished without a target, despite topping 100 yards in back-to-back games beforehand. Both wide receivers now have a big opportunity with Wilson out of the lineup against a Kansas City defense that's missing cornerbacks Mansoor Delane (shoulder) and L'Jarius Sneed (IR - knee).
injuryReports.injury: Mitchell and Omar Cooper will be the Jets' top wide receivers with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable for Sunday's game at Kansas City, ESPN's Rich Cimini reports.

injuryReports.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: After back-to-back 100-yard games in his first two weeks off injured reserve, Cooper ran 26 routes last week without registering a target in the 38-33 loss to Las Vegas. Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown, also running 26 routes, and Cimini's report notes that Mitchell "will become the No. 1 receiver" in Wilson's absence. Both Mitchell and Cooper figure to get plenty of snaps and routes, but targets and production aren't as assured.
injuryReports.injury: Cooper and Adonai Mitchell will be the Jets' top wide receivers with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable for Sunday's game at Kansas City, ESPN's Rich Cimini reports.

injuryReports.name: Breece Hall
injuryReports.returnComment: Hall has not taken the field since sustaining a quad injury in Week 3, but he practiced fully Thursday and appears primed to return to action Sunday. Braelon Allen has shined in Hall's absence, but Hall entered the season as the starter, so both figure to be involved to some degree in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Hall (quadriceps) "has been medically cleared" and is expected to play Sunday against the Chiefs, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

injuryReports.name: Dane Belton
injuryReports.returnComment: Belton was able to secure double-digit stops for the second time this season, finishing second on the team behind linebacker Jamien Sherwood (14). Belton is now up to 68 total tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding four passes defensed over eight contests to begin the regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Belton recorded 12 total tackles (eight solo) and a pass defensed in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Jamien Sherwood
injuryReports.returnComment: Sherwood notched a season-high 14 takedowns in the victory, securing double-digit stops for the third time in the last five contests. The linebacker has now compiled 68 total tackles (32 solo), four passes defensed, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery over eight games to open the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Sherwood recorded 14 total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: David Bailey
injuryReports.returnComment: After missing Week 8 with the groin injury he suffered the previous week, Bailey appears poised to return after missing just one contest. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 Draft, Bailey has piled up 35 tackles (21 solo), including 5.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and one pass breakup across seven starts this season.
injuryReports.injury: Bailey (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Mason Taylor
injuryReports.returnComment: Taylor was limited Wednesday, but his return to full Thursday puts him on track for his normal role Sunday against the Chiefs. The tight end has been a surprisingly big part of the passing offense this season despite the selection of Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of April's Draft. Taylor has secured 17 of 23 targets for 136 yards and two touchdowns across six games.
injuryReports.injury: Taylor (back) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Max Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: In a corresponding transaction, the Jets signed tackle Blake Freeland to their active roster. Mitchell, who has not made a start on the offensive line yet this season, will now have to miss at least the next four games.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: With Breece Hall (quad) missing another game, Davis handled RB2 duties behind workhorse Braelon Allen. Davis has totaled 15 carries for 44 empty yards this season, adding five catches for 68 yards. Hall is expected to return for Week 9 against the Chiefs, which would relegate Davis to the RB3 role.
injuryReports.injury: Davis rushed five times for 15 yards in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Kenyon Sadiq
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie tight end played 31 of 64 offensive snaps against Las Vegas and ran just 15 routes on Geno Smith's 35 dropbacks. Sadiq continues to play behind Mason Taylor, who recorded three grabs for 19 yards on five targets across 19 routes. The Jets are using four tight ends on game days, and this offense isn't able to support more than a couple pass catchers for fantasy each week. Outside of his 7-105-1 receiving performance in Week 3 against the Lions, Sadiq has a total of 10 catches for 79 yards across his seven other contests.
injuryReports.injury: Sadiq caught one of two targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Jason Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: Sanders made four shorter field goals from 21 yards, 36 yards, 39 yards and 31 yards in a perfect outing. The kicker worked to redeem himself after a crucial field-goal miss in a three-point loss to the Dolphins during Week 7. Sanders is 17-for-19 on field goals and 13-for-13 on PATs through eight 2026 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Sanders made all four of his field-goal attempts and three PATs in the Jets' 38-33 loss to the Raiders on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams ran a total of one route on Geno Smith's 35 dropbacks against Las Vegas, but he made it count with a red-zone touchdown. The Jets' fourth receiver behind Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper, Williams has no fantasy appeal headed into next Sunday's date with the Chiefs.
injuryReports.injury: Williams caught an 18-yard touchdown on his lone target in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Geno Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith threw second-quarter touchdown passes of 18 yards to Isaiah Williams and 12 yards to Adonai Mitchell while coming 10 yards shy of his second 300-yard passing performance of the season. The veteran QB had a chance to orchestrate a game-winning drive against his former team, but the Jets' comeback bid came up short when Smith threw an end-zone interception from the Raiders' 35-yard line with seven seconds remaining. Smith has been picked off in each of his last three outings after going without an interception through five starts to open his second tenure with the Jets. He'll take a 12:3 TD:INT into a Week 9 trip to Kansas City.
injuryReports.injury: Smith completed 20 of 32 passes for 290 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders. He also rushed once for four yards.

injuryReports.name: Dylan Parham
injuryReports.returnComment: Parham will be back in action for the first time since Week 3, when he sustained a knee injury in a loss to the Lions. Though he was listed as questionable heading into Sunday, Parham was cleared to play after logging a pair of limited practices and a full session during the week. He should step back in as the Jets' starting left guard, sending Jordan Meredith back to the bench.
injuryReports.injury: Parham (knee) is active for Sunday's game against Las Vegas.

injuryReports.name: T'Vondre Sweat
injuryReports.returnComment: Sweat was diagnosed with a knee injury during the Jets' Week 7 loss to the Dolphins. The initial diagnosis was week-to-week, and the Jets medical staff has determined that a stint on IR is warranted for the third-year defensive lineman, although he's expected to return this season. Sweat will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can play is Week 12 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 29, although he could be held out until after the Jets' Week 13 bye. Darrell Jackson and Harrison Phillips will both step into more prominent roles on the defensive line in Sweat's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Tanner McKee
injuryReports.returnComment: McKee has overcome his rib injury in time to suit up for Sunday's contest. The quarterback is set to back up Joe Milton against the Giants due to the absence of former starter Jalen Hurts (calf, IR).
injuryReports.injury: McKee (ribs) is active for Sunday's game against the Giants.

injuryReports.returnComment: inactive

injuryReports.name: Elijah Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: This marks Mitchell's third elevation of the campaign, meaning Philadelphia will need to sign him to the active roster after Week 9 if there's an expectation that he'll remain the team's No. 2 RB behind Saquon Barkley. With Barkley not operating at 100 percent last Sunday at Washington, Mitchell handled 57 percent of the snaps to the former's 32 percent, but Barkley's 14 touches went for 54 yards from scrimmage and one TD, while Mitchell produced just 37 total yards on 15 touches. The breakdown of work may skew more in Barkley's direction this week considering he entered the weekend without a designation for Sunday's matchup, but Mitchell figures to remains involved out of the Eagles backfield.
injuryReports.injury: The Eagles elevated Mitchell from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Jake Elliott
injuryReports.returnComment: Elliott was limited at practice Wednesday and Thursday due to an ankle issue, but he managed a full practice Friday and is in line to suit up Sunday. The Eagles have been arguably the most ineffective offense in the league so far in 2026, and there's not much reason to believe they'll turn things around in Week 9 against a solid Giants defense, leaving Elliott as an unappealing fantasy option.
injuryReports.injury: Elliott (ankle) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Darius Cooper
injuryReports.returnComment: Cooper made some big plays earlier this season but hasn't done much with his more recent opportunity, catching just three of nine targets for 36 yards over the past two weeks while playing 94 percent of snaps on offense. He's been targeted on just 13 percent of his routes this year, though that rate could improve some with strong-armed Joe Milton replacing Tanner McKee as the starting QB this week.
injuryReports.injury: Cooper and Makai Lemon are positioned to start again Sunday against the Giants, with fellow wideouts DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) ruled out for a third straight game, per PhiladelphiaEagles.com.

injuryReports.name: Makai Lemon
injuryReports.returnComment: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) both are out for a third straight game. Lemon led the team in targets the past two weeks, putting up receiving lines of 7-67-1 and 6-57-0 against the Cowboys and Commanders, respectively. He'll likely be a focal point of the passing game again, though Milton may be more inclined to look downfield toward Cooper or Hollywod Brown in situations where Tanner McKee would throw a shorter pass to Lemon or a TE/RB.
injuryReports.injury: Lemon and Darius Cooper profile as the top wide receivers for QB Joe Milton's first start in an Eagles uniform Sunday against the Giants, per PhiladelphiaEagles.com.

injuryReports.name: Saquon Barkley
injuryReports.returnComment: After sitting out Wednesday's session due to lingering hamstring and back injuries, Barkley ended Week 9 prep with back-to-back limited practices, which was enough to get the all-clear ahead of Sunday. He gutted out a 32 percent snap share this past Sunday in Washington en route to 14 touches for 54 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD while splitting the backfield with Elijah Mitchell (15 touches for 37 total yards).
injuryReports.injury: Barkley (hamstring/back) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Joe Milton
injuryReports.returnComment: Philadelphia signed Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad Oct. 16, and less than a month later, he's getting the call after the Tanner McKee experience so far has resulted in three consecutive losses. In five appearances (no starts) between New England and Dallas in his career, Milton has competed 37 of 53 passes for 424 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while rushing 15 times for 66 yards and one TD and losing both of his fumbles.
injuryReports.injury: Milton is set to be the Eagles' starting quarterback Sunday against the Giants, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.

injuryReports.name: Elijah Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: Moore was held without a catch for the first time since Week 5, failing to take advantage of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) being unavailable. Moore figures to remain an afterthought on offense in Week 9 against the Giants.
injuryReports.injury: Moore did not garner a target during Sunday night's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Hollywood Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: With both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) missing the contest, Brown ranked third among Eagles wideouts with 32 offensive snaps. He didn't do much with the opportunity, as the veteran wideout notched just two receptions for the second straight week. If Smith and/or Wicks return in Week 9 against the Giants, Brown may see his role diminish.
injuryReports.injury: Brown finished Sunday's loss to the Commanders with two catches for 17 yards on two targets.

injuryReports.name: Eli Stowers
injuryReports.returnComment: It was just the rookie's second game of the season after he debuted in Week 7 against Dallas. Stowers played on just 18.8 percent of the snaps against Washington, but he could earn more playing time by producing big plays when given the chance. In what's looking like a lost season for Philly, Stowers could be someone to stash in deeper fantasy leagues, especially if the Eagles trade Dallas Goedert ahead of next week's deadline.
injuryReports.injury: Stowers caught all three targets for 53 yards in Sunday night's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Jaydon Blue
injuryReports.returnComment: It was the running back's first action of the regular season after he was signed to the active roster last week. Blue logged eight offensive snaps and sits behind Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell on the depth chart. With Tank Bigsby (IR, abdomen) likely due back in the near future, Blue's stay on the 53-man roster could be short.
injuryReports.injury: Blue caught his lone target for nine yards in Sunday night's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Dallas Goedert
injuryReports.returnComment: Goedert has 15 catches for 139 receiving yards in three games since Tanner McKee took over as Philadelphia's starting QB, but the veteran TE has now gone five consecutive appearances without a TD after scoring 13 times in the span of 15 regular-season appearances through Week 1 of this season. Goedert had a ball bounce off his hands for an interception in the second half, but the play was negated by a defensive penalty, removing what would have been the lone blemish on Goedert's otherwise clean, though unimpressive, stat sheet. He'll try to snap his touchdown drought in Week 9 against the Giants.
injuryReports.injury: Goedert caught all four of his targets for 30 yards and added a two-yard run in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Nolan Smith Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith was a full participant in Friday's practice, and he was cleared from the league's concussion protocol after passing an evaluation by an independent neurologist. His return means less defensive snaps will be available for Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa.
injuryReports.injury: Smith (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Christian McCaffrey
injuryReports.returnComment: McCaffrey was limited to a 52 percent snap share when he missed a portion of the 49ers' Week 7 loss in Atlanta due to a left hamstring injury, but he still put up 13 touches for 100 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD. With the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he appears set to handle the 17.5 touches per game that he averaged in six healthy outings this season, which translated to 540 total yards and seven touchdowns.
injuryReports.injury: McCaffrey is expected to take on a full workload Sunday against the Raiders, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.

injuryReports.name: Mike Evans
injuryReports.returnComment: Evans is missing a second straight contest Sunday after aggravating a right Achilles injury during a Week 6 win against the Commanders. He hasn't been able to practice in the meantime, and while he's the type of player that doesn't require practice reps during the week to be available on game days, even work on the side Wednesday through Friday would be a welcome sign. In any case, with fellow WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring) also sidelined this weekend and Christian Kirk (knee) being placed on IR on Saturday, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing and KhaDarel Hodge are the options at the position to be active in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Achilles

injuryReports.name: Nate Hobbs
injuryReports.returnComment: Hobbs had his practice window opened Wednesday and logged three limited practices before initially being deemed questionable to face the Raiders on Sunday. Since he wasn't activated Saturday, the veteran cornerback will have to wait at least another week to return to action. Hobbs' next chance to do so is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Dallas.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: KhaDarel Hodge
injuryReports.returnComment: Hodge just signed with San Francisco's practice squad Monday, and he'll get an immediate chance to help the team's air attack. Starting wideouts Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) are both out for Sunday's matchup against Las Vegas, and Christian Kirk (knee) was placed on injured reserve Saturday. Therefore, Hodge figures to compete for WR snaps along with Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing, though Hodge could be last in the pecking order among that group.
injuryReports.injury: The 49ers elevated Hodge from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Christian Kirk
injuryReports.returnComment: Kirk made his season debut in San Francisco's last game in Week 7 in Atlanta, going without a target on a 30 percent snap share. After a Week 8 bye, he showed up on the initial Week 9 practice report Wednesday as limited due to a knee injury, which head coach Kyle Shanahan revealed to be to the wide receiver's meniscus Friday, per David Lombardi of SFStandard.com. Shanahan also relayed that Robinson may need surgery, but at the very least he'll miss the team's next four contests.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - Meniscus

injuryReports.name: Demarcus Robinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Robinson was carted off the field during the 49ers' Week 2 win against the Dolphins and was diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain, receiving a corresponding prognosis of 3-to-6 weeks on the sideline. After his placement on IR on Sept. 26, he missed the next five contests, but following a Week 8 bye, he was designated for return Wednesday and logged three straight limited sessions before being tagged as questionable. With his designation now a thing of the past, Robinson may immediately step into a prominent role in San Francisco's passing game Sunday due to fellow WRs Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) being out and Christian Kirk (knee) getting moved to IR.
injuryReports.injury: Robinson (ankle) was activated from injured reserve Saturday, per Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area, and the 49ers removed his questionable designation for Sunday's game versus the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Brandon Aiyuk
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Wagoner, Aiyuk submitted paperwork to be reinstated to the NFL in late October, and since then both the NFL Management Council and the NFL Players Association have been involved in an attempt to reach a resolution that's agreeable to both the wide receiver and the 49ers. Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported Thursday that Aiyuk's efforts to secure his release may be hampered by the roughly $13 million in bonus forfeitures that he owes the team, which could mean arbitration comes into play and delays the process. Friday's meeting between Aiyuk, his agent Drew Rosenhaus and San Francisco brass was only the first step. If the sides reach an agreement, the 49ers will have three options: release Aiyuk, trade him before Tuesday's deadline or add him to their 53-man roster.
injuryReports.injury: Personal

injuryReports.name: Garret Wallow
injuryReports.returnComment: Wallow was sidelined due to a strained hamstring in Weeks 6 and 7, but San Francisco's Week 8 bye gave him some extra recovery time. With an LP/LP/FP practice progression under his belt this week, the veteran linebacker is set to return to action against the Raiders. Wallow typically plays less than a quarter of the 49ers' defensive snaps, so he's not a recommended IDP option in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Wallow (hamstring) does not have a designation for Sunday's clash against Las Vegas.

injuryReports.name: Luke Gifford
injuryReports.returnComment: Gifford hurt his groin in Week 6 against Washington and didn't play in Week 7 versus Atlanta. However, San Francisco's Week 8 bye appears to have done him well, as the veteran linebacker returned to practice this week with an LP/LP/FP progression. Gifford has played primarily on special teams when healthy this season and will probably continue in that role against Las Vegas.
injuryReports.injury: Gifford (groin) does not have a designation for Sunday's Week 9 tilt against the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Marques Sigle
injuryReports.returnComment: Sigle missed the 49ers' last three games before their bye in Week 8 due to an ankle injury he sustained back in Week 4 versus the Broncos, but he's now set to get back on the field in Week 9. He projects to start at safety next to Ji'Ayir Brown against Las Vegas on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Sigle (ankle) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Nick Bosa
injuryReports.returnComment: Bosa was sidelined for the 49ers' last five contests before their bye in Week 8 because of a nagging knee injury, but after an extra week of rest, he'll return to action in Week 9. He might not get his full regular workload right away, but he should play a significant role on the edge Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Bosa (knee) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus Las Vegas.

injuryReports.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: With Samuel absent from the initial stage of practice Friday after sitting out Wednesday's and Thursday's sessions, he's trending toward an absence Sunday against the Raiders, as is fellow WR Mike Evans (Achilles). Confirmation of the duo's status is set to arrive later Friday once the 49ers' final Week 9 injury report is posted.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Siran Neal
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
injuryReports.returnComment: Stribling, who garnered his share of preseason fantasy buzz, was injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams, but it appears as though the wideout is making solid progress in his recovery. A firm timetable for the 2026 second-rounder's return to practice hasn't been outlined yet, but David Lombardi of SFStandard.com previously noted that Stribling (ankle) remains on track to return at some point in December, a notion supported by Barrows' report.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Dre Greenlaw
injuryReports.returnComment: Greenlaw missed Week 6 against Washington while on suspension but returned Sunday and logged a season-high 91 percent defensive snap share. The veteran linebacker tied his season high with 12 tackles, finishing one behind Fred Warner for the team lead. Greenlaw is enjoying a productive return to San Francisco with 49 tackles and a forced fumble through six contests.
injuryReports.injury: Greenlaw posted 12 tackles (four solo) in Sunday's loss to the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Fred Warner
injuryReports.returnComment: Warner led the 49ers in tackles, finishing one ahead of Dre Greenlaw. It was the fourth time through seven games that Warner has notched double-digit stops. The star linebacker ranks second in the NFL with 71 tackles through seven games.
injuryReports.injury: Warner recorded 13 tackles (six solo) Sunday in a Week 7 loss to Atlanta.

injuryReports.name: Brandin Cooks
injuryReports.returnComment: Cooks was in line to serve as the 49ers' top wide receiver for Week 7 due to the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Cooks' 45 offensive snaps were second-most among 49ers wideouts behind Jordan Watkins (50), although the former had only once catch to show for his extra playing time, which didn't happen until the final minute of the fourth quarter. Cooks has three catches (on seven targets) for 33 yards and a touchdown over his last three games, but his role could shrink significantly following the 49ers' Week 8 bye depending on the statuses of Evans, Samuel Christian Kirk and Demarcus Robinson (ankle, IR).
injuryReports.injury: Cooks caught one of three targets for 13 yards during Sunday's 29-20 loss to Atlanta.

injuryReports.name: Jacob Cowing
injuryReports.returnComment: Cowing and the other 49ers pass catchers operated in expanded roles Sunday due to the absences of both Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Cowing was on the field for 26 of the 49ers' 66 offensive snaps (39.4 percent), which was third most behind Jordan Watkins (50) and Brandin Cooks (45). Cowing put up season highs in catches, receiving yards and rushing yards, but his role could shrink significantly following the 49ers' Week 8 bye depending on the statuses of Evans, Samuel, Christian Kirk and Demarcus Robinson (ankle, IR), with rookie second-rounder De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle, IR) not expected back until December, per David Lombardi of SFStandard.com.
injuryReports.injury: Cowing caught three of five passes for 38 yards, added a 10-yard carry and returned one kickoff for 28 yards during Sunday's 29-20 loss to the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Jordan James
injuryReports.returnComment: Most of James' on-field work Sunday came on special teams. Both of his touches on offense happened on back-to-back plays in the second quarter, coinciding with the absence of Christian McCaffrey, the latter of whom was playing through a thigh injury during most of Sunday's contest. The only way James would see consistent playing time on offense is if one of McCaffrey or rookie Kaelon Black were to miss time. The 49ers will get some additional rest thanks to the Week 8 bye, and their next game takes place Week 9 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8.
injuryReports.injury: James logged a six-yard carry, turned his lone target into an 11-yard catch and registered 119 yards on four kickoff returns during the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Upton Stout
injuryReports.returnComment: Coach Kyle Shanahan said that Stout was only going to enter the game in an emergency scenario for the 49ers' secondary. The team hopes the Week 8 bye will allow Stout's shoulder sprain to fully heal ahead of the Week 9 showdown with the Raiders.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder - AC Joint

injuryReports.name: Brock Purdy
injuryReports.returnComment: Purdy put together an impressive passing yardage total, especially considering he was down both Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), along with De'Zhaun Stribling (IR, ankle) and Demarcus Robinson (IR, ankle). He also lost Christian McCaffrey for the entirety of the second quarter due to a leg injury that the star back eventually returned from, but the scarcity of his top pass catchers eventually led to a more mistake-filled performance than usual. The multi-interception tally was Purdy's first of the season, and the two picks led to 10 points for the Falcons. Purdy should have a chance to work with a deeper pass-catching corps in a Week 9 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8, as the Week 8 bye should offer multiple receivers a chance to recover from their respective injuries.
injuryReports.injury: Purdy completed 27 of 40 passes for 288 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions and added two carries for five yards in the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Juszczyk
injuryReports.returnComment: Juszczyk garnered multiple targets for the fifth straight game that he's played in, and he was able to reach paydirt for the second time this season, reeling in a one-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy in the fourth quarter. The fullback has yet to log a carry this season, and he's caught eight of 11 targets for 76 yards and two touchdowns over six contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Juszczyk caught all three of his targets for 11 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 29-20 loss to Atlanta.

injuryReports.name: Eddy Pineiro
injuryReports.returnComment: Pineiro went without a field-goal try for the second time this season, and he hasn't made multiple field goals in a contest since Week 1. To make matters worse, the kicker missed an extra-point try for the second straight week, and he's now 21-for-25 on PATs over the first seven games this season. With the 49ers off next week, Pineiro's next chance to be more involved will come in Week 9 against the Raiders.
injuryReports.injury: Pineiro did not attempt a field goal while going 2-for-3 on PATs in Sunday's 26-20 loss to the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Watkins
injuryReports.returnComment: With the 49ers' receiving corps down all of Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), De'Zhaun Stribling (IR, ankle) and Demarcus Robinson (IR, ankle), Watkins saw an expanded role and made good use of the opportunity. All three of Watkins' catches went for first downs, and he finished third on the team in receiving yards and targets while also tying for that slotting in receptions. The 2025 fourth-round pick's performance was encouraging, but he's likely to slide back down the depth chart since the wide-receiver room could be much healthier by the time San Francisco returns to action against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8, following the Week 8 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Watkins brought in three of six targets for 56 yards in the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Sam Darnold
injuryReports.returnComment: Darnold already has been ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Cardinals, and the combination of the quadriceps injury and cracked ribs he suffered last Monday against the Bears is threatening to sideline him for multiple weeks. The Seahawks have a Week 11 bye on the schedule, so getting him healthy for the stretch run from late November through early January may sway the team's decision-making. As long as Darnold is out, Drew Lock (right elbow) will direct Seattle's offense.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Montorie Foster Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Foster was also elevated last weekend, and he logged three snaps -- all on special teams -- against Chicago. Seattle was without Rashid Shaheed (knee) for that game and will be without him this Sunday against Arizona as well, but with the rest of the team's wideout corps in relatively good health, Foster probably won't see much action in Week 9 barring an injury or two ahead of him in the pecking order.
injuryReports.injury: The Seahawks elevated Foster from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Charles Cross
injuryReports.returnComment: Cross will miss his second straight game while tending to a high-ankle sprain he suffered in Week 7 against Kansas City. He wasn't able to participate in practice at all this week, and it's unclear when he'll be ready to return to the fold. Josh Jones could start again at left tackle in Cross's stead Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Brandon Pili
injuryReports.returnComment: Pili has missed four games this season, including last Monday's loss to Chicago. He'll be sidelined again this Sunday, as he's dealing with a back injury. Pili's absence probably won't make huge waves in the Seahawks' defensive rotations, as he's logged just 19 defensive snaps through four contests.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Uchenna Nwosu
injuryReports.returnComment: Nwosu sat out Monday's game versus the Bears with an ankle injury, and after missing practice Thursday and Friday, he'll miss his second straight game in Week 9. With Nwosu in street clothes, Derick Hall should start on the edge opposite veteran DeMarcus Lawrence on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Leonard Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams was not able to practice at all during the week after hurting his shoulder during Monday's game versus the Bears, and he'll be sidelined for his first contest this season in Week 9. In his absence, Mike Morris projects to see an increase in snaps on the defensive line.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Ernest Jones IV
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones popped up on the Seahawks' injury report with an ankle issue Thursday, but he was able to log a full practice Friday and is on track to play Sunday. He is the NFL's third leading tackler on the season going into a Week 9 contest against a pass-heavy Cardinals offense.
injuryReports.injury: Jones (ankle) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus Arizona, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Quenton Nelson
injuryReports.returnComment: Nelson is set for knee surgery due to an issue the veteran offensive guard has been having with cartilage fragments.  Ian Rapoport of NFL Network said Friday that the plan is for Nelson to avoid IR and return to the Seahawks after the team's Week 11 bye. Grey Zabel is set to start at left guard for Sunday's game.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Drew Lock
injuryReports.returnComment: Lock logged three consecutive limited sessions this week due to the right elbow injury that has relegated him to inactive status as the emergency third quarterback the last two games. However, with his status now cleared up for Week 9 action, he's set to fill in for Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) for at least one contest. In two previous appearances (one start) in place of Darnold in Weeks 1 and 2, Lock completed 35 of 48 passes (73 percent) for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions and had two carries for 13 yards. Jalen Milroe will back up Lock on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Lock (right elbow) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the Cardinals, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Rashid Shaheed
injuryReports.returnComment: With Shaheed out last week, Tory Horton handled a 72 percent route share in Seattle's loss to Chicago. It'll likely be a similar look this week with Horton and Cooper Kupp taking most of the WR snaps alongside Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The big difference will be under center, where Drew Lock is filling in for Sam Darnold (quad) for the second time this season.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Connor O'Toole
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Jalen Milroe
injuryReports.returnComment: Milroe is expected to serve as the top backup behind Drew Lock at quarterback in Week 9 with Sam Darnold (quadriceps) sidelined. Milroe has yet to appear in a regular-season contest this season and likely won't do so Sunday unless Lock is forced out of the contest with an injury.
injuryReports.injury: Milroe will get added reps at practice ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Cardinals, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.

injuryReports.name: Tory Horton
injuryReports.returnComment: Horton was on the field for 43 of the Seahawks' 63 offensive snaps, with his 68 percent share representing a season high. The six targets were also a season-best total for Horton, who was the main beneficiary of extra playing time due to the absence of Rashid Shaheed (knee). If Shaheed is cleared to play in the Seahawks' Week 9 game against the Cardinals, Horton will likely see his role get reduced.
injuryReports.injury: Horton recorded three receptions for 26 yards on six targets in Monday's 34-17 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: George Holani
injuryReports.returnComment: With the Seahawks clearing Zach Charbonnet (knee) to make his season debut and with Jadarian Price (chest) coming off injured reserve, Holani predictably saw his playing time out of the backfield take a hit. He was on the field for just 11 of the Seahawks' 63 offensive snaps, with his season-low 17 percent snap share placing him comfortably behind Price (48 percent) and Charbonnet (37 percent) but ahead of Emanuel Wilson (zero snaps). For the first time all season, Holani was called upon to serve as the Seahawks' primary kickoff returner, as Rashid Shaheed (knee) and Velus Jones (hamstring) were inactive Monday.
injuryReports.injury: Holani carried once for nine yards and failed to haul in his lone target in Monday's 34-17 loss to the Bears. He also returned six kickoffs for 144 yards.

injuryReports.name: Emanuel Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: After logging double-digit carries in six of the Seahawks' previous seven games while scoring four touchdowns and averaging 66.4 scrimmage yards during that span, Wilson fell out of the game plan entirely in Week 8. With Zach Charbonnet (knee) getting cleared to make his 2026 debut, Jadarian Price (chest) returning from injured reserve and George Holani still on hand as an option on passing downs, the Seahawks had no reps available out of the backfield for Wilson. Unless Charbonnet or Price succumbs to another injury, Wilson's playing time on offense will likely remain scarce moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson played just seven snaps -- all on special teams -- in Monday's 34-17 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: AJ Barner
injuryReports.returnComment: Barner was third in receiving yards and targets, although the tight end still finished below 30 receiving yards for the sixth time this season. He remained in a minor role despite the fact the Seahawks were down Rashid Shaheed (knee), and with 21 receptions for 203 yards and zero touchdowns, the third-year pro remains behind the pace of his career-best 52-519-6 line from last season. Barner will look to capitalize on a favorable matchup against the Cardinals defense in a Week 9 home matchup on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Barner brought in two of five targets for 23 yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Zach Charbonnet
injuryReports.returnComment: Charbonnet took the first carry of the night for Seattle, gaining an encouraging five yards on his first tote since tearing his left ACL in a divisional-round win over the 49ers in January. He also subsequently rattled off a 13-yard gain in the third quarter, but he was limited on his other touches and ultimately had four fewer rush attempts than Jadarian Price. Charbonnet's snap share and touches should gradually increase, and a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals could serve as a good platform for his workload to see a nice bump.
injuryReports.injury: Charbonnet (knee) rushed six times for 23 yards and brought in three of four targets for six yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Cooper Kupp
injuryReports.returnComment: Kupp had another low target share, but he at least made the most of his only catch by hauling in a seven-yard TD early in the fourth quarter. That score probably isn't going to be enough to inspire confidence in him in fantasy, though, given that the veteran wideout has drawn three or fewer targets in six of his eight games this season. Kupp's seven receiving yards Monday also were a season-low mark, and there simply doesn't seem to be much room for any wideout aside from Jaxon Smith-Njigba to regularly find success in Seattle's offense given Smith-Njigba's massive target share. With that said, Kupp at least will have a favorable matchup in Week 9, as he'll face an Arizona defense that has surrendered 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this season, tied for the most in the NFL.
injuryReports.injury: Kupp caught one of three targets for a seven-yard touchdown Monday in a loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Jason Myers
injuryReports.returnComment: Myers converted a chip-shot 27-yard field goal in the second quarter but later missed an extra point wide to the left before halftime. He then had a 33-yard field-goal try blocked in the fourth quarter. On the season, the veteran kicker is 14-for-16 on FGAs and 17-for-19 on PATs. He'll be a kicker to stream next Sunday at home against the Cardinals.
injuryReports.injury: Myers missed his lone field-goal attempt and made one of two PATs in Monday night's 34-17 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Jadarian Price
injuryReports.returnComment: Making his return from a four-game stay on injured reserve due to a chest injury, Price ended up leading the Seahawks' ground attack in carries and rushing yards. Price's return coincided with the season debut of Zach Charbonnet (knee), who logged six carries in his own right in a game whose script eventually turned unfriendly to the running game. Monday may have served as a preview of what might be expected in terms of the division of labor between the two players, but more information will be gleaned during a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday that should afford both backs more opportunities.
injuryReports.injury: Price rushed 10 times for 29 yards and brought in two of four targets for eight yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith-Njigba was in his usual position of leading the Seahawks across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and he crossed the 100-yard mark for the seventh time in eight games this season with a pair of catches on Seattle's final drive of the night. His target total also was his sixth double-digit tally of the campaign, and the absence of Rashid Shaheed (knee) helped reinforce JSN's downfield role even further. Smith-Njigba now will head into a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday just 15 yards short of his third consecutive 1,000-yard campaign and only a touchdown shy of tying the career-high 10 he recorded over 17 regular-season games last season.
injuryReports.injury: Smith-Njigba brought in six of 11 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Emeka Egbuka
injuryReports.returnComment: On the heels of two games on the sideline due to a concussion and a foot injury, Egbuka kicked off this week as a non-participant Wednesday before logging back-to-back full sessions Thursday and Friday. Despite clearing the protocol for head injuries ahead of Week 8 action, he was listed as questionable with the foot issue ahead of Sunday's matchup, but Pelissero's report indicates Egbuka is trending toward active status. Egbuka's availability will be clarified approximately 90 minutes before an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Tristan Wirfs
injuryReports.returnComment: Wirfs appeared on Thursday's injury report as a non-participant with a toe injury. The star left tackle managed to upgrade to limited for Friday's session. The upgrade to limited participation was enough to clear Wirfs of any injury designation, and the veteran protector is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest.
injuryReports.injury: Wirfs (toe) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Tykee Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith was limited at practice by an ankle issue Wednesday and Thursday, but he managed to practice in full Friday and will avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend. He projects to start at safety next to Antoine Winfield in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Smith (ankle) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Josiah Trotter
injuryReports.returnComment: Trotter was limited by an illness at practice ahead of Week 8, and he ultimately secured a season-low six stops in the win. The rookie linebacker has put together quite the impressive start to his first NFL campaign, compiling 68 total tackles (32 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding a pick-six over seven contests so far.
injuryReports.injury: Trotter recorded six total tackles (two solo) during Sunday's 16-0 victory over Atlanta.

injuryReports.name: Jacob Parrish
injuryReports.returnComment: Parrish was able to notch multiple passes defensed for the fifth straight game, and he was able to reel in his second interception of the year, jumping in front of a short pass from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix in the second quarter. The cornerback has now compiled 36 total tackles (30 solo) and 13 passes defensed, including two interceptions, over seven contests so far during the 2026 regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Parrish registered seven total tackles (four solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 16-0 win over Atlanta.

injuryReports.name: Alex Anzalone
injuryReports.returnComment: Anzalone was able to secure exactly six takedowns for the second straight week, but his biggest impact came in the passing game. The linebacker intercepted Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix twice in the first quarter, jumping in front of short passes intended for Drake London and Jahan Dotson. Anzalone has now registered 42 total tackles (17 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also notching a career-high three interceptions over eight games so far during the 2026 regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Anzalone recorded six total tackles (three solo) and two interceptions in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Kenny Gainwell
injuryReports.returnComment: Gainwell also tended to a hip injury last week, when he got back to full by Friday, but he still entered the weekend listed as questionable for Week 8 action. He proceeded to suit up this past Sunday against the Falcons and split Tampa Bay's backfield with Bucky Irving, logging a 50 percent snap share and going for 140 yards on 25 carries in rainy conditions. Considering Gainwell followed up Wednesday's limited session with an uncapped one Thursday, he's good to go for Sunday's road showdown with the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: Gainwell (hip) was a full practice participant Thursday, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jalen McMillan
injuryReports.returnComment: McMillan was initially given a return timetable of 6-to-8 weeks after aggravating a PCL sprain in his left knee in Week 3. Head coach Todd Bowles said McMillan won't have his window to return from IR opened before the Buccaneers face the Bears on Sunday, and Tampa Bay will be on bye the following week, so McMillan's next chance to play won't come until Nov. 22 at Detroit.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - PCL

injuryReports.name: Bauer Sharp
injuryReports.returnComment: After logging single-digit snaps on offense in each of the first six games of the season, Sharp appears to have firmly supplanted Ko Kieft as the Buccaneers' No. 3 tight end behind Cade Otton and Payne Durham. Sharp played a quarter of the snaps in a Week 7 win over the Buccaneers before bumping up to a season-high 32 percent share during Sunday's victory. The rookie sixth-round pick out of LSU will likely continue to be utilized mainly as a blocker; he's drawn just one target (a 21-yard reception) while running only nine total routes so far this season.
injuryReports.injury: Sharp went without a target while playing 19 of the Buccaneers' 60 snaps on offense in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Tez Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson and the rest of the Buccaneers' pass catchers went without receptions in Week 8 as quarterback Baker Mayfield failed to complete a pass on three attempts in the team's rain-soaked victory. The wide receiver may have another chance to operate in a prominent role on offense if fellow wideout Emeka Egbuka (foot) remains unavailable Sunday versus the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson did not garner a target during Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Ted Hurst III
injuryReports.returnComment: Even with Emeka Egbuka (foot) missing a second straight game, Hurst couldn't catch a break, as the game was played in a downpour. Tampa Bay attempted just three passes during the entire game. Hurst has now gone without a catch in back-to-back games without Egbuka in the lineup. Hurst has minimal fantasy appeal outside of being a hold in dynasty formats.
injuryReports.injury: Hurst failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Sean Tucker
injuryReports.returnComment: The Bucs' RB3 played one snap on special teams. He stayed glued to the sideline, as Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell ran roughshod all over the Atlanta defense, combining for 52 carries, 310 yards and one touchdown. Tucker won't hold much fantasy value unless one of Irving or Gainwell goes down with an injury.
injuryReports.injury: Tucker didn't play any offensive snaps in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Cade Otton
injuryReports.returnComment: Playing in rain-soaked conditions, the Bucs attempted just three passes all afternoon, as Baker Mayfield failed to complete any of the three. Otton now has posted back-to-back zero-catch games and has minimal fantasy appeal outside of the deepest of TE-premium formats. He has 19 grabs for 186 yards and no touchdowns on 30 targets through eight games.
injuryReports.injury: Otton wasn't targeted in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Chase McLaughlin
injuryReports.returnComment: The kicker connected from 46, 34 and 42 yards as he accounted for a majority of his team's points. McLaughlin has yet to miss this season, hitting 19 field goals and 17 extra points through eight games.
injuryReports.injury: McLaughlin made all three field-goal attempts and his only extra-point try in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Yaya Diaby
injuryReports.returnComment: Diaby exited this past Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons with the knee injury, which was revealed to be a Grade 2 MCL sprain following an MRI on Monday, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Though Diaby will miss at least one game due to the injury, Bowles expressed hope that the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye would aid the edge rusher's recovery and allow him to avoid a stint on injured reserve.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - MCL

injuryReports.name: Baker Mayfield
injuryReports.returnComment: The afternoon-long rainy conditions in Tampa Bay and the Falcons' defense's complete inability to slow down the Buccaneers' ground attack led to Mayfield barely putting in any work as a passer. In the process, the Bucs became the first team since 1974 to win a game without a single completion, and the bizarre circumstances left Mayfield's fantasy managers with a dead spot in their lineups. Mayfield will naturally be a lot busier when he travels to the Windy City to face the Bears' aggressive defense in a Week 9 road showdown next Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Mayfield failed to complete any of his three pass attempts in the Buccaneers' 16-0 win over the Falcons on Sunday. He also rushed four times for 14 yards.

injuryReports.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The Bucs attempted three total passes in Sunday's rain-soaked conditions, and Baker Mayfield didn't complete any of the three. Instead, Tampa Bay ran the ball 56 times and coasted to an easy win on the backs of Bucky Irving, Kenny Gainwell and the defense. Godwin will do battle with the Chicago secondary next Sunday, positioning the veteran wideout as a WR4 in fantasy. Emeka Egbuka (foot) could be back for that game after missing the past two contests.
injuryReports.injury: Godwin failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Bucky Irving
injuryReports.returnComment: The Buccaneers became the first team since 1974 to win a game without completing a single pass, so Irving was somewhat of a one-man wrecking crew as far as the offense was concerned. The talented running back's yardage total was a career-high figure, and the performance was the third of over 100 yards for Irving already this season. The third-year back added his fifth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a four-yard run to close out the scoring with 3:47 remaining, and Irving is now up to 728 rushing yards and 5.0 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Bears next Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Irving rushed 27 times for 170 yards and a touchdown in the Buccaneers' 16-0 win over the Falcons on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Luke Goedeke
injuryReports.returnComment: Goedeke earned the questionable tag for Week 8 after logging a limited practice Friday, and he's been cleared by medical staff to return from a one-game absence due to a calf injury. He'll reclaim his starting spot at right tackle while Benjamin Chukwuma reverts to a depth role.
injuryReports.injury: Goedeke (calf) is active for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Graham Barton
injuryReports.returnComment: Barton picked up an illness over the weekend, but the third-year center has been cleared to play Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Barton (illness) is active for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Josh Hayes
injuryReports.returnComment: Hayes underwent a minor procedure on his knee after getting hurt in the preseason, and there's currently no timetable for his return following the setback. Once healthy, the 27-year-old should contribute on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Antoine Winfield Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Winfield has been sidelined for the Buccaneers' last three games while nursing a rib injury. He showed enough progression in his recovery to log a full practice Wednesday, which puts him on track to play against the Falcons on Sunday. Winfield should reclaim his starting role at safety, so Ifeatu Melifonwu figures to revert to a rotational role in the secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Winfield (ribs) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Brianna Dix of the Buccaneers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Athan Kaliakmanis
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie seventh-round pick will continue to operate as Washington's third quarterback behind Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota. Both QBs would need to be forced out of the game for Kaliakmanis to see the field.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Jer'Zhan Newton
injuryReports.returnComment: The 24-year-old was reinstated from injured reserve Saturday but was still officially questionable to play Sunday versus Los Angeles. Newton is ready to make his season debut after recovering from surgery to repair a torn pectoral muscle in August.
injuryReports.injury: Newton (pectoral) is active for Sunday's game against the Rams.

injuryReports.name: Jaden Bradley
injuryReports.returnComment: Bradley is being elevated for the first time since joining Washington's practice squad in September. The 23-year-old should provide the team with additional depth at receiver against the Rams, as both Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf) have been ruled out due to injury.
injuryReports.injury: The Commanders elevated Bradley from their practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's matchup versus the Rams.

injuryReports.name: Dyami Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Brown will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a calf injury during Thursday's practice. With Treylon Burks (foot) also ruled out, Van Jefferson and Luke McCaffrey could see increased usage on offense during Sunday's matchup versus the Rams.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Daron Payne
injuryReports.returnComment: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that Payne will be out long-term with a foot injury suffered in practice. With both Javon Kinlaw (knee) and Payne out, Tim Settle will have a larger role at nose tackle going forward.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Jeremy McNichols
injuryReports.returnComment: McNichols was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, and what coach Dan Quinn described as a "serious mid-foot injury" will keep the running back sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) slated to miss at least two more games, the Commanders' current healthy RBs are Rachaad White, Austin Ekeler and Robert Henry.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Javon Kinlaw
injuryReports.returnComment: Washington placed Kinlaw on injured reserve Tuesday, but it wasn't immediately known how much time the knee injury he initially sustained Week 6 would keep him out of commission. Now that Kinlaw has opted for surgery, he'll remain on IR for the Commanders' final 10 games in what amounts to another major hit to the defensive line. Washington also placed nose tackle Daron Payne on IR on Tuesday after he needed surgery to repair a Jones fracture in his left foot.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - MCL

injuryReports.name: Robert Henry Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: After being cut by Seattle on Monday, Henry quickly caught on with the Commanders. The 2026 undrafted free agent out of UTSA had previously joined the Commanders for training camp and the preseason, only to be waived prior to Week 1. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on injured reserve for at least two more games and Jeremy McNichols (foot) likely to miss the remainder of the season, Henry will provide the Commanders with another option in the backfield behind Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler. Henry didn't end up making his NFL debut during his time on the Seahawks roster.
injuryReports.injury: The Commanders claimed Henry off waivers from the Seahawks on Tuesday.

injuryReports.name: Drew Stevens
injuryReports.returnComment: Stevens had just one blemish in an otherwise great game in Week 8, as he missed a 55-yard attempt after the Commanders' first drive of the game. Regardless, he set a new career high in field goals made in a game. Washington's offense will try to keep up the momentum against a tougher defense in Week 9 versus the Rams.
injuryReports.injury: Stevens made four of his five field-goal attempts and converted his only extra-point try during Sunday's 27-10 win versus the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Chig Okonkwo
injuryReports.returnComment: Okonkwo logged a typical 77 percent snap share in Week 8, but aside from a stellar 21-yard catch in the fourth quarter, he didn't contribute much to the Commanders offense. Overall, he's mustered just a 17-182-0 line on 24 targets in his five appearances this season, but 15 of his catches have occurred in the four full contests for Jayden Daniels in 2026, so the tight end has exhibited a rapport with the team's primary signal-caller. Okonkwo will aim for a bounceback this coming Sunday against the Rams.
injuryReports.injury: Okonkwo tallied two catches (on four targets) for 32 yards during Sunday's 27-10 win versus the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Antonio Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams led the team in catches and targets while finishing second behind fellow wide receiver Treylon Burks (81) in receiving yards. With Terry McLaurin (knee) done for the year, Williams will have an opportunity to keep carving out a larger role for himself each week with Washington. On the year, the rookie wide receiver has now reeled in 23 of 33 targets for 259 yards and one touchdown over seven regular-season contests.
injuryReports.injury: Williams caught five of seven targets for 54 yards during Sunday night's 27-10 win over the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Austin Ekeler
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran running back wasn't targeted in the passing game on a night when Jayden Daniels attempted 29 passes. Involved in a three-way backfield that also includes Rachaad White and Jeremy McNichols (foot), Ekeler has minimal fantasy appeal headed into next Sunday's matchup with the Rams' strong defense. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (foot) is required to miss at least one more game on injured reserve.
injuryReports.injury: Ekeler rushed eight times for 36 yards in Sunday night's 27-10 win over the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Rachaad White
injuryReports.returnComment: Most of White's production came during a three-play span on Washington's final possession, as he ripped off a 33-yard run down to the four-yard line, followed by a three-yard gain and a one-yard touchdown run to put the game out of reach. The Commanders have divided up backfield duties while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is on IR, as Austin Ekeler notched eight carries, while Jeremy McNichols (foot) had five carries and one catch prior to exiting in the second half. White continues to have the highest touch floor among Washington's available running backs heading into Week 9 against the Rams, and he has scored in three of the last four games, with the previous two touchdowns both coming on receptions.
injuryReports.injury: White rushed 11 times for 55 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for five yards in Sunday's 27-10 win over the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Stefon Diggs
injuryReports.returnComment: Diggs scored an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter, and the ensuing PAT tied the score at 10-10. That was the team-leading fifth receiving touchdown for Diggs in six appearances with the Commanders. He's the top option for Jayden Daniels on paper since Terry McLaurin sustained a season-ending knee injury in Washington's previous game, though Treylon Burks (81) and Antonio Williams (54) both had more receiving yards Sunday, and Williams also drew one more target than Diggs to lead the team. Diggs is poised to maintain a prominent role in Week 9 against the stout Rams secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Diggs caught three of six targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-10 win over the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Jayden Daniels
injuryReports.returnComment: Daniels found Stefon Diggs for an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter and led four drives that ended in successful field goals before Rachaad White sealed the deal with a one-yard touchdown run late in the fourth quarter. Diggs has been on the receiving end of four of Daniels' six touchdown passes this season. Daniels threw for 300 yards in a Week 6 loss to the 49ers prior to Washington's Week 7 bye, but he hasn't exceeded 233 passing yards in any of his 11 other regular-season outings since the start of the 2025 campaign. Sunday night's win over Philadelphia marked Daniels' first win since Week 5 of the 2025 season, when Washington defeated the Chargers. The Commanders will take a 2-4-1 record into a Week 9 home game against the Rams.
injuryReports.injury: Daniels completed 16 of 29 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown while rushing twice for 23 yards in Sunday's 27-10 win over the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Charles Omenihu
injuryReports.returnComment: Omenihu will return to action in Week 8 after missing two straight contests with a pair of groin and ankle injuries. The 29-year-old will be back in a prominent role on the defensive line versus Philadelphia.
injuryReports.injury: Omenihu (groin/ankle) is active for Sunday night's contest against the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Terry McLaurin
injuryReports.returnComment: The surgery was conducted in New York, and McLaurin has already been ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season. His availability for the start of the 2027 campaign will also be in question, as the veteran wideout faces a lengthy rehab process. The Commanders will move forward with Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown and Treylon Burks atop the wideout depth chart this season.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

His usage could be similarly limited Sunday against Seattle, as the Cardinals have three healthy tight ends (Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Teagan Quitoriano) ahead of Bowman in the pecking order.

sources.returnComment: Ford signed with Arizona's practice squad Oct. 14 and is now set to potentially make his gameday debut with the team Sunday in Seattle. He spent his first four NFL campaigns with Cleveland and averaged an acceptable 4.3 yards per carry with seven rushing touchdowns over 340 totes while also accumulating 647 yards and an additional five touchdowns on 107 catches across 57 games. Given that level of experience, it will be interesting to see how much the Cardinals utilize Ford on Sunday, though Tyler Allgeier is slated to work as the team's lead back, and Evan Hull will also factor into the mix.

sources.name: Elijah Higgins
sources.returnComment: Wideout Michael Wilson missed a portion of the contest due to an injury to his ribs, and Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) exited for good late in the first half. That resulted in a need for other Cardinals pass catchers to step up, and Higgins ended up getting targeted a season-high four times. However, he didn't do much with the opportunity, finishing with his lowest yardage total since he was shut out in Week 2. Meanwhile, No. 1 tight end Trey McBride had another big game with seven catches for 72 yards and a touchdown on eight targets. McBride's elite status will likely continue to make Higgins an afterthought most weeks.

Duvernay will likely see an increased role on offense in Bourne's absence, but he will remain an unappealing fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup against Seattle.

00-0036646.label: Active
00-0036646.injury: Fehoko is listed as a starting receiver on the Cardinals' unofficial depth chart heading into Sunday's game at Seattle, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.

sources.name: Simi Fehoko
sources.returnComment: Buried on the depth chart at receiver to begin the season, Fehoko mostly served as a special-teams contributor through the Cardinals' first seven games. However,the Cardinals have since traded away Marvin Harrison before losing Jalen Brooks (wrist) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) to season-ending injuries within the past two weeks, so Fehoko suddenly finds himself in a position to contribute. Fehoko played double-digit snaps for the first time in 2026 on Sunday, coincidentally against his former teams the Cowboys. He wasn't much of a factor in a comeback win, however, earning just one target for a 17-yard reception while taking the field for 40 of the team's 81 offensive play. While Fehoko could see his playing time climb even higher in Week 9, tight ends Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins, wideout Michael Wilson (ribs) and running back Tyler Allgeier may be better bets to command targets from quarterback Gardner Minshew.
sources.injury: Fehoko is listed as a starting receiver on the Cardinals' unofficial depth chart heading into Sunday's game at Seattle, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.

sources.name: James Conner
sources.returnComment: Though LaFleur said last week that Conner could "potentially" play this season, that won't happen in Week 9. The veteran running back continues to work his way back from a right foot injury and has not yet been cleared to practice. Arizona is dealing with multiple injuries in its backfield, including Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion), so Conner could provide a big boost once he's able to work his way back this week. Instead, the team will turn to Tyler Allgeier to lead its backfield, with Evan Hull serving as his primary backup if Knight is unable to suit up Sunday against Seattle.
